Ridership/Performance Notes: High adoption in Fox Valley

Name: SMTD Micro

Name: MCRide

Name: SCCTD Flyer

Name: Connect FLEX

Ridership/Performance Notes: Serves student and local populations

Name: MTD SafeRides
Fleet: Nighttime on-demand service focusing on student safety.
Ridership/Performance Notes: High university student usage

Name: MetroLINK On-Demand
Fleet: Replaced underperforming fixed routes in low density areas with on-demand.

Name: RIDES Mass Transit

Ridership/Performance Notes: High elderly/medical usage

Name: SCT Demand Response
Fleet: Regional DAR. Same day allowed if capacity permits.

Name: JCMTD On-Demand
Fleet: County-wide on-demand transit. Same day booking available.
Ridership/Performance Notes: Mix of students and rural

Name: Shawnee MTD
Fleet: Rural demand response serving southernmost Illinois.

Name: WCMTD Dial-A-Ride
Fleet: Accommodates same-day rides based on schedule availability.

Name: Piattran
Fleet: Countywide transportation. Same day requests taken if available.

Name: Ride in Kane
Fleet: Coordinated paratransit/DAR. 24h notice typical but same-day accommodated.
Ridership/Performance Notes: Seniors and disabled focus

Name: Salem Skipper
Fleet: Public microtransit service launched Dec 2020. Expanded to Danvers and Peabody. Connects to MBTA commuter rail.
Ridership/Performance Notes: Averaging hundreds of rides per week.

Name: GATRA GO
Region/Service Area: Plymouth, Franklin, Foxborough, Mansfield, Norfolk, Wrentham, Pembroke, Marshfield
Operator: Greater Attleboro Taunton Regional Transit Authority (GATRA)
Fleet: Replaces fixed routes in lower-density zones. Divided into Coastline, United, and Seacoast zones.
Ridership/Performance Notes: High adoption in Plymouth area.

Name: CATA On Demand
Fleet: Replaced traditional dial-a-ride service to offer same-day, app-based booking for general public.
Ridership/Performance Notes: Not specified

Name: NewMo (Newton in Motion)
Fleet: Replaced traditional senior transport, expanded to all residents. First mile/last mile to MBTA.
Ridership/Performance Notes: Highly successful, hundreds of daily rides.

Name: SmartDART
Fleet: App-based on-demand service augmenting fixed routes on Cape Cod.
Ridership/Performance Notes: Very popular during summer tourist season.

Name: WRTA Via
Fleet: Piloted in Westborough to serve office parks and MBTA commuter rail, extended based on demand.
Ridership/Performance Notes: Steady ridership growth.

Name: Tri-Town Connector
Region/Service Area: Great Barrington, Stockbridge, Egremont, Sheffield, Monterey
Operator: Tri-Town Board of Health / Local Transit
Fleet: Rural microtransit model connecting Southern Berkshire towns without fixed bus routes.
Ridership/Performance Notes: Serving critical transit-desert populations.

Name: Quaboag Connector
Operator: Town of Ware / Quaboag Valley CDC
Fleet: Initially advance booking, shifted to accommodate same-day local trips for healthcare and jobs.
Ridership/Performance Notes: Critical for rural transit access.

Name: MeVa On Demand
Fleet: Replaced underperforming fixed routes with Spare Labs-powered on-demand vans.
Ridership/Performance Notes: High ridership due to zero-fare policy.

Name: CrossTown Connect
Fleet: Centralized dispatch for several towns' COA and general public dial-a-rides. Offers same-day dispatch.
Ridership/Performance Notes: Solid municipal partnership model.

Name: MART OnDemand
Fleet: MART integrates traditional dial-a-ride with same-day microtransit in select outer zones.
Ridership/Performance Notes: Not specified.

Name: FRTA Microtransit
Fleet: Rural microtransit pilot addressing low-density first/last mile gaps in Franklin County.
Ridership/Performance Notes: Growing slowly due to rural nature.

Name: VTA On Demand
Fleet: Off-season and evening microtransit replacing empty fixed-route buses during lower demand periods.
Ridership/Performance Notes: Efficient seasonal adjustment.

Name: Valley Transit Demand Response
Region/Service Area: Matanuska-Susitna (Mat-Su) Borough, AK — zoned areas of the Valley (Wasilla, Palmer, Houston, Big Lake, Meadow Lakes, Knik-Goose Bay, Fairview, Port MacKenzie, Butte)
Fare: $3 general public per zone traveled; $2 seniors 60+ and youth 17 & under per zone
Ridership/Performance Notes: Point-to-point zoned curb-to-curb demand-response open to the general public; bookable up to ~2 weeks in advance; reported ~24,700 riders/year with daily waitlists.

Name: BRATS On-Demand
Region/Service Area: Baldwin County, AL (countywide; Eastern Shore, Foley, Robertsdale, Bay Minette, Gulf Shores areas)
Operator: Baldwin County Commission - Baldwin Regional Area Transit System (BRATS)
Fare: Distance-based (each way): 0-5 mi $2.00, 6-10 mi $2.50, 11-15 mi $3.00, +$0.50 per additional 5 mi
Ridership/Performance Notes: Public door-to-door shared-ride on-demand service. Same-area trips available ASAP; can book up to 7 days in advance (per official site). Launched Sept 2020 via FTA Integrated Mobility Innovation (IMI) grant originally with Via; now operates on Spare platform. Wheelchair-accessible vehicles available on request.

Name: MAX On-Demand (formerly Birmingham On-Demand)
Region/Service Area: Birmingham & Jefferson County, AL microtransit zones: Downtown/City Center, East/Airport, North Birmingham, Mountain Brook, Homewood (Irondale pilot); ~26.6 sq mi core coverage
Operator: Birmingham Jefferson County Transit Authority (MAX Transit); previously City of Birmingham; powered by Via
Fare: $1.50 flat per shared ride; $0.75 per additional passenger
Service Hours: Varies by zone (e.g. Downtown Mon-Fri 6am-7pm, Sat 10am-6pm; East/Airport Mon-Sat 5am-9pm)
Funding Source: Local (City of Birmingham), Federal (FTA); Greater Birmingham Community Foundation grants for Homewood/Irondale pilots
Fleet: Not specified (Via-branded vans; wheelchair-accessible vehicles available)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Corner-to-corner shared microtransit launched 2019 under City of Birmingham/Via; Sept 2025 City Council transferred the program and $2.5M in funding to BJCTA/MAX Transit and rebranded it MAX On-Demand; expanded into suburban zones (Mountain Brook, North Birmingham) and July 2026 15-month pilots in Homewood ($792K) and Irondale ($513.75K). Max trip ~3.5 miles.

Name: MoGo Rideshare
Region/Service Area: 17-mile service zone, City of Mobile, AL (workforce/employment corridors)
Operator: Mobile Area Chamber of Commerce Foundation, operated by Via
Fare: Free to employment/training centers (AIDT, Airbus, Austal USA, FlightPath9); $1.25 to other destinations
Funding Source: Federal (Carbon Reduction Program via South Alabama Regional Planning Commission), Local (City of Mobile), Community Foundation of South Alabama, Alabama Power Foundation, Blue Cross Blue Shield Caring Foundation
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launched March 16, 2024 as workforce-access pilot; corner-to-corner shared rides with virtual stops; received over $500,000 in Carbon Reduction Program grants. Being incorporated into a redesigned Via-led Mobile transit network launching July 2026.

Name: The M: Micro Transit
Region/Service Area: City of Montgomery, AL — mapped zones incl. Downtown Montgomery, Montgomery Regional Airport, Montgomery Whitewater, Maxwell AFB Visitor Center, Jackson Hospital
Fare: $1.50 per ride (promotional; credit/debit or exact cash to driver)
Ridership/Performance Notes: On-demand shared rideshare; requests booked in real time with short wait times, or scheduled up to 7 days in advance; open to general public; complements fixed-route bus.

Name: METRO Connect
Region/Service Area: Central Arkansas zones: John Barrow Road, Riverdale, Levy-Amboy, East Little Rock, Hensley (Little Rock); North Little Rock; Sherwood; Conway
Operator: Rock Region METRO (Central Arkansas Transit Authority)
Fare: Standard METRO fares (cash, passes, Token Transit; Conway zone exact cash or virtual 1-Ride passes only)
Ridership/Performance Notes: On-demand, point-to-point-within-zone shared microtransit connecting to fixed-route transfers; started 2020 with a John Barrow test zone, since expanded to eight zones; migrated from TransLoc to Via platform; walk-up bookings eliminated Oct 2023; Conway public zone launched Oct 2024.

Name: ORT On-Demand
Region/Service Area: Northwest Arkansas city zones: Fayetteville, Springdale, Rogers (Mon-Sat); Bentonville (Sat only)
Fare: $1.25 per trip for up to 5 riders in a group
Ridership/Performance Notes: App-based on-demand shared rides (door-to-door) within defined zones around NWA cities; may direct riders to fixed routes when faster. Program began in Rogers ~2020 and expanded to Bentonville/Fayetteville Feb 2022 (2 buses each in Rogers/Bentonville at that time); ride requests grew from ~500/week (Feb 2022) to ~1,500/week (Jul 2022).

Name: DART Connect
Region/Service Area: Three on-demand zones: Georgetown and Millsboro (Sussex County) and Newark (New Castle County), DE
Operator: Delaware Transit Corporation (DART First State), a division of DelDOT
Booking Method(s): App (DART Transit / DART Connect app), Phone (1-800-652-DART, Option 3)
Fare: $2.00 per ride (same as DART bus fare); day/week/30-day/20-ride passes available
Service Hours: Newark: Mon-Fri 6am-8pm; Georgetown & Millsboro: Mon-Fri 5:45am-8pm; no service on DART holidays
Fleet: Minibuses / mini-transit buses (~11 seats each; Newark launched with two vehicles)
Ridership/Performance Notes: State's first on-demand microtransit. Georgetown/Millsboro launched Apr 12, 2021 as an FTA-funded pilot replacing Flex Routes 901/902; continued after pilot success. Newark added Aug 2023, replacing the Unicity fixed-route loop. Waits estimated no more than 15 min. Available to the general public; first/last-mile connections to regular DART routes.

Name: Hele-On Ka Hoʻokele (Rural Door-to-Door Service)
Region/Service Area: Rural areas outside Hele-On fixed routes: Seaview/Kalapana, Upper Puna, Waimea, Hilo, Kailua-Kona, Captain Cook; Island of Hawaiʻi
Operator: Hawaiʻi County Economic Opportunity Council (HCEOC), operating for the County of Hawaiʻi Mass Transit Agency
Service Hours: Monday-Friday 7:30 AM to 4:30 PM, excluding County-observed holidays
Funding Source: Local (County of Hawaiʻi Mass Transit Agency)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Open to the general public who reside in rural areas outside regular fixed-route and paratransit coverage. Registration required; reservations at (808) 731-7009 option 3, minimum one day in advance, up to 14 days ahead. Riders travel within a district or are taken to the nearest Hele-On fixed-route stop for onward travel.

Name: DART On Demand
Region/Service Area: Des Moines metro — Ankeny microtransit zone (active); Clive, Urbandale and Altoona zones planned fall 2026 under Reimagine DART
Operator: Des Moines Area Regional Transit Authority (DART)
Fare: $3.50 standard; $0.75 half-fare and children ages 6-10; pay via DART On Demand app, myDART app, DART pass/tokens, or exact change
Service Hours: Ankeny zone: Monday–Friday 6:00 a.m.–6:30 p.m. (last trip booking 6:15 p.m.)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Point-to-point on-demand shared rides within a defined zone using smaller buses; trips can be booked in real-time or scheduled in advance and may be shared. Ankeny zone runs as-is until Sept 28, 2026, then reconfigured Ankeny plus new Clive-Urbandale and Altoona zones launch fall 2026 under Reimagine DART. Ankeny zone bounds: NE 62nd Ave (south), SE Four Mile Dr (east), 36th St (north), SW Irvinedale Dr (west).

Name: EASE (East Ames Service Extension)
Region/Service Area: East Ames on-demand zone, Ames, IA (pickups within EASE zone plus Ames City Hall)
Operator: CyRide (City of Ames / Iowa State University transit)
Fare: $1.00 per trip (same as regular CyRide bus fare)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Curb-to-curb on-demand service; riders use the Ride Pingo app or call CyRide (515-239-5600, at least 30 min ahead for call-ins). Pingo platform launched with CyRide Dec 2022 — The Routing Company's first Midwest on-demand agency partnership. Two-year TRC contract awarded Oct 2022; agency reported improved efficiency, reduced call-center volume, high rider satisfaction. Transfers to fixed routes at City Hall.

Name: HIRTA On-Demand
Region/Service Area: Boone, Dallas, Jasper, Madison, Marion, Story and Warren counties (central Iowa)
Operator: Heart of Iowa Regional Transit Agency (HIRTA)
Service Hours: Mon-Fri 7:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. (Story County from 6:30 a.m.)
Fleet: ADA-accessible / wheelchair-lift-equipped vehicles (fleet size not specified)
Ridership/Performance Notes: General public, any trip purpose; same-day or advance booking; pickups within a 20-minute window, door-to-door across seven counties. HIRTA is an FTA ITS4US complete-trip deployment site.

Name: Peoplerides
Region/Service Area: Hardin, Marshall, Poweshiek and Tama counties, Iowa
Fare: In-town $2-$15 depending on county/city; out-of-town demand-response $2.89 per mile
Ridership/Performance Notes: Established 1974; open to the general public including persons with disabilities; provides 50,000+ rides annually across the four counties using 20 ADA-accessible vehicles; offers both route and demand-response trips. Advance booking (at least one day) receives priority; same-day depends on driver availability. Medicaid-funded trips booked via broker (MTM); Marshalltown paratransit requires prior approval.

Name: Region 8 Regional Transit Authority (RTA) On-Demand
Region/Service Area: Delaware, Dubuque (excl. City of Dubuque) and Jackson counties, northeast Iowa (Planning Area 8)
Fleet: ~30 light-duty buses and accessible minivans; transitioning to 9-passenger vans
Ridership/Performance Notes: Modernized rural demand-response using QRyde booking/routing/scheduling platform; ~100,000 passenger trips annually serving ~2,500 individuals. Advance reservations typically requested 24h ahead; same-day available subject to availability; ~10-min-out arrival notifications. Open to the general public; all vehicles wheelchair accessible.

Name: River Bend Transit
Region/Service Area: Cedar, Clinton, Muscatine and Scott counties (Iowa Quad Cities region)
Fare: Not specified (varies by county/contract; per-county fare cards; same-day trips at premium; veterans ride free)
Service Hours: Varies by service; Bettendorf Dial-A-Bus Mon-Fri 6 a.m.-6 p.m., Sat 8:45 a.m.-5:40 p.m.
Ridership/Performance Notes: Iowa's first regional consolidated transit system (est. 1978); general-public door-to-door demand-response serving seniors, people with disabilities, and the general public across the Iowa Quad Cities; also offers same-day service (premium fare), county services, low-income employment transportation, and contracted city services (e.g. Bettendorf Dial-A-Bus). FTA transit agency profile ID 70049.

Name: SEIBUS (Southeast Iowa Bus)
Region/Service Area: Des Moines, Henry, Lee and Louisa counties, southeast Iowa
Fare: $3.00 in-town one-way; $15–$30 medical shuttle; monthly passes offered by county (per Iowa DOT / SEIBUS)
Service Hours: Monday–Friday, 6:00 AM–4:00 PM (county availability windows ~9:00 AM–3:00 PM)
Fleet: Wheelchair-lift-equipped buses; fleet size not specified
Ridership/Performance Notes: On-demand curb-to-curb demand-response with no fixed routes; open to the general public including persons with disabilities; advance booking required — appointments must be made no later than 2:00 PM the day prior to departure (no same-day). Iowa DOT classifies it as Demand-Response, Subscription. Ridership figures not found.

Name: SWITA (Southwest Iowa Transit Agency)
Region/Service Area: Cass, Fremont, Harrison, Mills, Montgomery, Page, Pottawattamie and Shelby counties, SW Iowa
Service Hours: Mon-Fri 6:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. (vehicles operate 24/7 pending availability)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Public on-demand rideshare open to all residents of eight SW Iowa counties; also offers student, medical, work-route, taxi and excursion services. On-demand rides 6a-5p weekdays.

Name: Siouxland Regional Transit System (SRTS)
Region/Service Area: Cherokee, Ida, Monona, Plymouth and Woodbury counties (IA); southern Union County, SD; Dakota County, NE
Service Hours: Mon-Sat 5:30 a.m.-7:00 p.m.; closed major holidays
Fleet: ADA-accessible buses (seat belts); fleet size not specified
Ridership/Performance Notes: Demand-responsive, ADA-accessible public transit open to the general public; curb-to-curb and door-to-door service; reservations requested ~24 hours in advance by phone.

Name: Trip Connect (Johnson County)
Region/Service Area: Iowa City, Coralville, University Heights, North Liberty, Tiffin, and all parts of Johnson County north of I-80 (evening service)
Operator: Horizons NTS (Neighborhood Transportation Service), contracted by Johnson County Social Services
Funding Source: Local (Johnson County, City of North Liberty, Kirkwood Community College), State (Iowa DOT special projects grant), National Center for Mobility Management grant, passenger revenue
Ridership/Performance Notes: Curb-to-curb on-demand or scheduled evening rides for workers/students; launched Dec 11, 2024; completed 4,200+ rides; pilot ended June 30, 2026 due to ~$350k/yr funding shortfall.

Name: SMART Transit Dial-A-Ride
Region/Service Area: Twin Falls and Jerome area (south-central Idaho)
Operator: SMART Transit (South Central Community Action Partnership)
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public Dial-A-Ride demand-response; priority given to ADA riders and seniors 60+, then general public. Phone reservations only; same-day reservations not accepted (advance booking required). Shared-ride, ADA wheelchair accessible, fare-free.

Name: Access Johnson County Public Transit
Region/Service Area: Johnson County, IN (zone-to-zone countywide; Franklin, Greenwood, etc.)
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public demand-response ('Demand Response and Flexible Fixed Route service'); reservations by phone (317-738-5523) or the 'Trip Portal' smartphone app for registered riders; all vehicles wheelchair accessible; ADA paratransit certification available separately.

Name: BLink
Region/Service Area: Within Bloomington city limits (Downtown, East, and North zones); serves trips not within walkable distance of a fixed bus route
Fare: $2 per one-way trip; pay in-app, cash (exact change), Tap To Pay, or Umo card
Ridership/Performance Notes: No eligibility or application required; rides booked on demand or up to 24 hours in advance. Repeated no-shows/late cancellations may result in booking restrictions.

Name: Hamilton County Express
Region/Service Area: Hamilton County, IN (Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Westfield and contiguous counties)
Service Hours: Mon-Fri 6:00am-6:00pm; Sat 7:00am-3:00pm; closed major holidays (booking line Mon-Fri 8am-4pm)
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public demand-response (reservation-based) transit in Hamilton County; open to individuals with disabilities and the general public; connects to contiguous counties. Booking via 317-773-2688.

Name: METS Micro
Region/Service Area: City of Evansville, Indiana (designated on-demand zones; expanding to Jacobsville)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launched Nov 27, 2023; completed over 37,000 rides by first anniversary (Nov 2024). Powered by Via; supported by Toyota Mobility Foundation, Evansville MPO, and Energy Systems Network. Curb-to-curb; booking by app or phone (812-562-5011). Expanding to Jacobsville.

Name: Lawrence Transit On Demand
Region/Service Area: City limits of Lawrence, Douglas County, KS (curb-to-curb, citywide zone)
Operator: Lawrence Transit (City of Lawrence / University of Kansas partnership)
Fare: $3 one-way (credit/debit only, no cash), effective March 1, 2026
Service Hours: Daytime: 8 a.m.–6 p.m. Sunday; Nighttime: 8 p.m.–6 a.m. Mon–Sat and 12 a.m.–6 a.m. Sunday
Fleet: Smaller buses, all ADA accessible and equipped with bike racks (count not specified)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Curb-to-curb on-demand shared-ride service open to the general public, book any two points in town; booked via Lawrence Transit On Demand app (Spare, iOS/Android) or phone (785) 312-7054. Ridership/performance data not published on site.

Name: Night Line
Region/Service Area: Within Lawrence city limits, Douglas County, KS
Fare: $2 cash only per trip (passes not accepted)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Evening/overnight curb-to-curb on-demand service open to the general public; rides scheduled by phone in advance during business hours (8 a.m.–5 p.m.) rather than fixed-stop. Originally launched as a one-year pilot on June 1, 2013; still listed as a core Lawrence Transit service.

Name: LYNX Microtransit (CATS LYNX)
Launch Year: 2022 (approximate — sourced from a 'reported 4-year partnership' reference as of March 2026, not a confirmed exact date)
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public, on-demand microtransit in Baker zone; CATS materials cite award recognition and cumulative ridership near 430,000 rides across LYNX + growing ADA paratransit service (combined figure, not LYNX-only). CATS also runs a separate 'CATS on Demand' service (~10,000 rides/month) whose relationship to LYNX is unclear from available sources.

Name: River Parishes Transit Authority (RPTA) On-Demand Service
Region/Service Area: St. Charles, St. James, and St. John the Baptist parishes, LA
Technology Vendor: Not specified (branded as "Link-Microtransit" booking platform; underlying vendor company not confirmed)
Funding Source: Not specified (RPTA created by Louisiana legislation as a regional transit authority; funding mechanism not confirmed)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Live booking portal (fetched directly) confirms an on-demand ride service in the three river parishes; riders must call dispatch (985-233-4339) before their first booking, then book via app/phone. Portal text states a 'pre-booking is required...based on available schedules,' which is somewhat ambiguous — could not fully confirm a pure no-fixed-schedule same-day model vs. a windowed reservation system. Fare/hours/fleet/vendor/funding not confirmed this pass.

Name: SporTran OnDemand
Fleet: Not specified (Dodge Caravans, Chevy Malibu and Dodge Challenger sedans mentioned, no total count)
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public on-demand service branded 'Powered by the RideCo Transit App'; zone-based with designated stops, service area shown on interactive map; also used for ADA-eligible trips but not restricted to them.

Name: Lynx (Penquis Transportation)
Region/Service Area: Penobscot and Piscataquis Counties, ME (excluding Patten)
Fare: Varies by distance traveled; no general-public pass offered
Service Hours: Not specified (service operates at least one day per week in each town within its area)
Fleet: Agency vans, volunteer drivers, and taxi services (fleet size not specified)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Demand-response transportation serving Penobscot and Piscataquis Counties (excluding Patten), operated by the Penquis community action agency. Requires 3 business days' advance notice to schedule a ride. Open to the general public, with additional coordinated services for elderly, MaineCare recipients, veterans, and people with disabilities. Contact: 207-973-3695 or 1-866-853-5969.

Name: Metro Connect (Falmouth)
Operator: Greater Portland Metro (GPMetro / Greater Portland Transit District)
Service Hours: 7 days/week, circulating within Falmouth service zone (specific start/end times not specified)
Funding Source: Federal (ARPA) -- per 2024 GPMetro RFP for the on-demand transit pilot program; not explicitly reconfirmed in later coverage
Ridership/Performance Notes: GPMetro's first microtransit program; door-to-zone on-demand shuttle open to the general public, booked through the Spare Rider platform (vendor confirmed via booking URL). Per a Nov 2025 one-year-in review, averaging ~1 ride/hour with a goal of 2 rides/hour by end of 2025. Service area has expanded to cover most of Falmouth since a December 2024 launch.

Name: Mid-Coast Connector (WCAP Transportation Services)
Region/Service Area: Waldo, Knox, Lincoln, and Sagadahoc Counties, plus Brunswick and Harpswell, ME (fixed-route DASH service separately in Belfast/Rockland)
Fare: Not specified (varies by service type/distance; reduced fares for seniors, children under 17, and disabled riders reported for DASH and senior medical trips)
Ridership/Performance Notes: WCAP operates flex-route/demand-response service open to the general public plus MaineCare non-emergency medical transportation, distinct from its fixed-route DASH city bus service in Belfast/Rockland. Confirmed via Maine Transit Association member listing and WCAP's own program page.

Name: RTP (Regional Transportation Program)
Region/Service Area: Cumberland County, Maine (includes Lakes Region Explorer route between Bridgton and Portland)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Shared-ride demand-response service prioritizing elderly, disabled, and low-income riders but explicitly open to the general public; requires advance phone booking (same-day changes must be called in, not made online). Separately offers ADA-compliant paratransit (ADA Rider Application/Policy) not separately catalogued here.

Name: RTP Catch-A-Ride
Fare: $2.50 (same town/neighboring towns), $5.00 (non-adjoining towns); many riders qualify for free service via application
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public, county-wide shared-ride demand-response service; RTP states it serves 'anyone' in Cumberland County on a space-available basis. NOT disability-restricted -- that description (people 'prevented by a disability from utilizing fixed-route bus service') applies to RTP's separate ADA paratransit program, not Catch-A-Ride. Booking is phone-only (774-2666 or 800-244-0704); no app booking found on the source page despite candidate's 'Phone, App' claim. Requires up to 2 weeks advance booking, minimum 2 business days notice -- not same-day.

Name: Standish-Gorham Microtransit Pilot
Region/Service Area: Standish and Gorham (RTP also serves Raymond, Windham, and a separate Harrison pilot), Cumberland County, ME
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launched October 15, 2025; same-day on-demand home pickup to any destination within service area. Funded through at least May 2026, with a $6 fare extension to downtown Portland reportedly proposed. Distinct from RTP's separate Harrison pilot ($99,576 grant) and from RTP's general advance-reservation (2+ business days) demand-response/paratransit service.

Name: Western Maine Transportation Services (WMTS)
Region/Service Area: Androscoggin, Oxford, and Franklin Counties, plus Bath and Brunswick, ME
Ridership/Performance Notes: Demand-response service open to the general public across three western Maine counties plus Bath/Brunswick; site also lists separate flex, fixed, and commuter routes (not in scope). Fares reported unchanged since Oct 1, 2019 (amount not specified).

Name: GEST (Liberty/Gladstone, MO)
Region/Service Area: Liberty, MO and Gladstone, MO (Northland Kansas City region); candidate also lists North Kansas City, Riverside, Parkville — unverified
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public, door-to-door, on-demand service; replaced a discontinued IRIS microtransit service (IRIS ended late Sept 2025 due to rising costs). Liberty launched ~1 week before article, Gladstone ~1 month prior; Liberty saw a 140% week-over-week ridership increase and up to 50 rides/day expected; Gladstone completed 'hundreds of rides.' Liberty is running a 30-day pilot before deciding on contract extension. Vehicles are NOT ADA-compliant — riders needing accommodation are directed to Liberty Access Bus or separate GEST paratransit option. Some riders reported being unable to book rides despite operator claims of full availability.

Name: IRIS (Independence)
Region/Service Area: City of Independence, MO (entire city limits)
Operator: City of Independence (funder/project manager) / Kansas City Area Transportation Authority (KCATA, service manager) / zTrip (operations) / RideCo (technology)
Fare: $5.00 per person per trip (free to/from 4 designated transfer points: Independence Transit Center, Centerpoint Medical Center, Independence Municipal Commons, Blue Ridge transfer point)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Dynamic-routing microtransit covering entire Independence city limits, pickup/dropoff within ~1/4 mile of requested locations. Candidate's original fare ($3.00) and fleet ('Not specified') were incorrect/incomplete per official city source; corrected here. One secondary April 2025 news report suggested planned cessation May 1 2025, but the live official city page (checked July 2026) states the service is currently active — worth flagging in concerns.csv if added. Launch year conflicting (candidate: 2023; one news summary: Jan 2025) and unconfirmed from a primary source, left as Not specified.

Name: OATS Transit (OATS, Inc.)
Region/Service Area: 87 counties across rural Missouri (statewide, excludes core areas of major metros like St. Louis and Kansas City)

Ridership/Performance Notes: Town-wide on-demand service with no fixed schedule; part of MOOver's Southeast Vermont microtransit family alongside MicroMOO2 (Brattleboro) and Springfield Microtransit. Distinct from MOOver's fixed-route service.

Name: DC Neighborhood Connect
Region/Service Area: Wards 1, 4, 5, and 8, Washington, DC (DFHV cites expanded coverage possibly including Ward 6) — multiple defined service zones connecting neighborhoods to Metrorail stations
Funding Source: Local (District of Columbia government — e.g. $1.034M FY2021, $1.7M FY2022 appropriations)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Zero-fare, app/phone-booked shared on-demand shuttle operated by DFHV (not DDOT — candidate's original operator/website attribution to DDOT was incorrect) using Via technology, connecting DC neighborhoods within designated zones to Metrorail stations and activity centers. Confirmed via a 2022 mayoral press release announcing expansion into Northwest and Northeast DC. Vendor, fare, and operator now independently verified; launch year, hours, and fleet still need sourcing.

Name: Casper Area Transit — ASSIST (Dial-A-Ride)
Region/Service Area: City of Casper, WY (candidate's claim of Bar Nunn/Evansville/Mills coverage unverified)
Fare: General public: $5.00/ride; Honored Citizen (age 62+, disabled, Medicare cardholder): $2.50; children 2-12: $1.00; children under 2 with car seat: free
Service Hours: Reservations taken by phone Mon-Fri 8:00am-12:00pm and 1:00pm-5:00pm; limited holiday service 7:30am-1:30pm on select dates (actual ride-service hours not separately confirmed)
Fleet: Not specified (all vehicles described as lift-equipped/ADA accessible, no count given)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Successor to Casper Area Transportation Coalition (CATC); City of Casper assumed operations May 7, 2021 after financial mismanagement findings at CATC (unverified by this check, retained from candidate). Confirmed via official site: ASSIST is open to honored citizens (62+), people with disabilities, AND the general public — it is not an eligibility-restricted paratransit-only service, contrary to the candidate's original framing.

Name: START On-Demand
Region/Service Area: Town of Jackson, Teton County, WY
Operator: START (Southern Teton Area Rapid Transit) / Town of Jackson
Ridership/Performance Notes: Free on-demand ride service within the Town of Jackson; no fixed routes or schedules. Booking via smartphone app or phone (307-400-4438). START overall (fixed-route + on-demand) reported roughly 1,035,000 total passengers in 2024, first time above pre-COVID levels, but this figure was not confirmed to be On-Demand-specific.

Name: Wind River Transportation Authority (WRTA)
Region/Service Area: Fremont County, WY (Riverton, Lander, Wind River Indian Reservation), central Wyoming
Funding Source: Federal (FTA 5311 Rural Transportation Grant, FTA 5339 Bus and Bus Facilities Grant), State (WDOT Highway Safety Office), Other (LOR Foundation, Donations)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Curb-to-curb On-Demand service is one of three WRTA programs alongside Fixed Route and the SafeRide late-night program; agency traces to 1989 (as SANTA), renamed WRTA in 1996 under Fremont County governance. Open to general public, not eligibility-restricted.

Name: Murray-Calloway Transit Authority On Demand
Region/Service Area: Murray / Calloway County, KY (Purchase area, Southwest Kentucky)
Booking Method(s): Phone (270-753-9725), confirmed via MCTA FAQ; a rider app via Pantonium's "EverRun" platform was claimed by the source candidate but could not be independently confirmed — not mentioned on MCTA's own site
Fare: City ride $2 (advance) / $5 (same-day); County ride $4 (advance) / $7 (same-day); out-of-zone $2.00/mile; wait time $15/hr; shared-ride runs to Mayfield/Benton $15/person, Paducah $20/person (confirmed via services-and-pricing page; City/County Pass and children-free details not independently re-verified but same source)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Branded "City and County On Demand" service, confirmed open to the general public ("It's for Everybody!"). Same-day, no-fixed-schedule phone-booked service confirmed directly on murraytransit.com. Distinct from TANK Plus (different operator/region: Northern KY/Cincinnati metro vs. Murray/Calloway in far western KY). Vendor/app claim (Pantonium EverRun) in the original candidate notes was NOT corroborated during this verification pass — MCTA's website makes no mention of an app or dispatch vendor — recommend confirming via Google Play listing or direct outreach before publishing that detail.

Name: Cecil Transit Demand Response
Technology Vendor: Via (ridewithvia.cac.ceciltransit app package name; not independently confirmed via Via/county press materials this session)
Booking Method(s): Mobile app (Cecil Transit, ridewithvia.cac.ceciltransit) or phone (410-996-5295, option 2)
Fare: Mileage-based fare; cash (exact change) at boarding, or prepaid Ride Credit via cash, check, or money order
Service Hours: Monday-Friday, 8am-4pm; closed county holidays and severe weather days
Ridership/Performance Notes: Countywide origin-to-destination demand-response service open to all ages (children under 13 require an accompanying adult) on a first-come, first-served basis — no senior/disability eligibility restriction, distinct from Cecil Transit's separate ADA paratransit service. Excludes county holidays and severe weather days.

Name: Dorchester County Transit (DCT)
Fare: $3.00 one-way general public; $1.50 one-way seniors (60+) and persons with disabilities
Fleet: Wheelchair-accessible buses (accommodate wheelchairs, power scooters, mobility devices); count not specified
Ridership/Performance Notes: Operates fixed-route plus door-to-door demand-response service; door-to-door requires 24-hour advance notice and is open to the general public (not eligibility-restricted), with reduced fare for seniors/disabled riders. Operated by Delmarva Community Services, Inc., a nonprofit, not Dorchester County government directly as the candidate stated (correcting that field). Service area described on DCT's own page spans Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, and Talbot Counties, which may indicate a shared regional operator footprint rather than county-exclusive service -- worth flagging in concerns.csv if other Upper/Mid-Shore counties get separate entries later to avoid double-counting the same underlying operator/fleet.

Name: Garrett Transit Service (GTS)
Operator: Garrett County Community Action Committee (GCCAC), Inc.
Booking Method(s): Phone dispatch (301-533-9010), Monday-Friday 7:00 AM-6:00 PM; after-hours voicemail reviewed next business day
Fare: In-county: $3.00-$7.00 per trip based on distance and rider type (ambulatory vs. senior/disabled); tickets sold in $10/$20 booklet increments. Out-of-county: starts at $40, priced per mile.
Service Hours: Monday-Friday (service days); scheduling calls accepted 7:00 AM-6:00 PM
Funding Source: Not specified (community sponsors noted: United Way, Community Trust Foundation, First United Bank; no state/federal grant program confirmed)
Fleet: Wheelchair-accessible buses and vans (accommodate up to 32-inch-wide wheelchairs, 800 lbs capacity) with portable oxygen tank accommodation; fleet size not specified
Ridership/Performance Notes: Shared-ride, door-to-door countywide demand-response service open to general public with accommodations for seniors and persons with disabilities. Local trips require min. 24-hour advance notice; out-of-county trips require min. 3-day notice. Out-of-county destinations include Frostburg MD, Terra Alta WV, Bruceton Mills WV, Dulles Airport, Washington DC, Johnstown PA, and Pittsburgh PA (candidate's list of Baltimore/Hagerstown/Frederick/Morgantown/Cumberland not independently corroborated but plausible given service's regional reach).

Name: HoCo RapidRide
Region/Service Area: Howard County, MD (Route 1 corridor: Elkridge, Jessup, Savage, Hanover, Columbia)
Operator: Howard County Office of Transportation (Howard County Government), implemented in collaboration with Via
Booking Method(s): App (HoCo RapidRide app, iOS/Android); phone booking available at 443-348-9572 for riders without smartphones
Fare: $2 per ride; free for HCPSS students, community college students, and seniors 60+ with valid ID; first month free through April 17, 2025 as a launch promotion
Funding Source: $500,000 Maryland Statewide Transit Innovation Grant plus $530,000 Howard County matching funds
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launched March 17, 2025 under County Executive Calvin Ball. Shared-ride van service using corner-to-corner (not door-to-door) pickup/dropoff model; connects Route 1 corridor communities (Elkridge, Jessup, Savage, Hanover, Columbia) to shopping destinations (Dobbin Center, Snowden Square, Gateway Overlook) and other local destinations. Riders must be at least 13 (younger with parent/guardian).

Name: PGC Link
Region/Service Area: Prince George's County, MD (Fort Washington-Oxon Hill-Accokeek zone; expansion proposed for Bowie, Hyattsville, and Laurel zones)
Operator: Prince George's County Department of Public Works & Transportation (TheBus)
Fare: Free as of June 30, 2025 (county-wide fare waiver for TheBus, PGC Link, and Call-a-Bus); previously $2 via TransLoc app only, cash/tokens/SmarTrip not accepted
Ridership/Performance Notes: Original zone covers Fort Washington-Oxon Hill-Accokeek and is confirmed operating. Additional zones (Bowie, Hyattsville, Laurel, and a split South County/National Harbor zone) appear on PGC's ArcGIS microtransit hub as proposed/planned expansion zones, not yet confirmed live. Fare was originally $2 via the TransLoc app but Prince George's County waived fares on TheBus, PGC Link, and Call-a-Bus as of June 30, 2025, per the City of Hyattsville's transportation page. Direct fetch of the county's own PGC Link page returned HTTP 403 during verification; findings rely on a DuckDuckGo search snippet of that page plus the Hyattsville city government confirmation.

Name: Queen Anne's County Ride
Operator: Queen Anne's County Department of Aging
Ridership/Performance Notes: MTA LOTS directory (state DOT source) lists Queen Anne's County Ride as operated by the County Department of Aging, offering 'deviated-fixed route and demand response service' to 'the general public, older adults, and people with disabilities' — general-public eligibility is explicit for the demand-response component, distinguishing it from a paratransit-only service. Only the demand-response component is in scope; the deviated-fixed-route service is excluded. Secondary aggregator sources (211md.org, iCarol) corroborate the program's existence and describe County Ride broadly as free to residents with added specialized services for seniors/disabled, but do not confirm demand-response-specific fare, hours, booking method, or scheduling window. Official qac.org pages for the service returned 404 on every URL tried (qac.org/198/Transportation, qac.org/162/County-Ride); no working official website located. Operator name corrected from candidate's 'Queen Anne's County Government' to the more specific verified 'Queen Anne's County Department of Aging' per LOTS.

Name: Ride On Flex
Region/Service Area: Montgomery County, MD (Zone 918 — Sandy Spring/White Oak, New Hampshire Ave corridor)
Operator: Montgomery County Department of Transportation (Ride On)
Booking Method(s): App (Ride On Flex app, iOS/Android) or phone call to 240-301-3842; call center hours Mon-Fri 6am-7pm
Ridership/Performance Notes: As of July 1, 2026 the Rockville and Glenmont/Wheaton zones were discontinued; only Zone 918 (Sandy Spring/White Oak, along New Hampshire Ave from Cloverly St to Lockwood Dr/White Oak Center) continues operating. Same-day on-demand booking only, no fixed schedule. Not to be confused with fixed-route Ride On bus service. Won a 2020 NACo Innovation Award.

Name: Shore Ride (Shore Transit)
Region/Service Area: Wicomico, Worcester, and Somerset Counties, MD (Lower Eastern Shore)
Operator: Shore Transit (Tri-County Council for the Lower Eastern Shore of Maryland)
Booking Method(s): Phone reservation via Shore Transit Customer Service Center (443-260-2300)
Fare: $5.00 per ride (general public); $4.00 per ride for elderly/disabled riders in Wicomico County
Service Hours: Not specified (operates during fixed-route service hours, which vary by county)
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public rural demand-response service for riders who live 3/4 mile or more beyond a fixed-route stop or transfer point, across the 3-county Lower Eastern Shore service area (Somerset, Wicomico, Worcester). Requires reservation by noon the day prior to travel. Distinct from Shore Transit's separately branded 'Shore Access' ADA origin-to-destination paratransit service (also $5/ride, restricted to riders whose disability prevents fixed-route use).

Name: DJ Transit (Southern Connect)
Fleet: Buses, vans, and wheelchair-accessible (ADA-compliant) vehicles; fleet size and capacity not specified
Ridership/Performance Notes: Community transportation provider based in Laurel, MS (1010 Rogers Street). Site confirms rides must be scheduled at least 24 hours ahead by phone, open to general public for work, school, shopping, business, and medical trips. Branded 'Southern Connect' on MDOT's ConnectMS regional network page, which independently confirms the same phone number and describes the region as serving 13 counties in south Mississippi. Buses serve employment/school/senior routes within Jones County; vans and wheelchair-accessible vehicles serve broader medical/shopping/recreational trips. Fare details exist only in a downloadable PDF/PPT not retrievable via fetch.

Name: Delta Rides
Region/Service Area: Northwest Mississippi Delta (21 counties per MDOT ConnectMS)
Operator: Regional network of nonprofit transportation providers in the Mississippi Delta, coordinated via a shared call center under MDOT's ConnectMS program (37 partner agencies including transit agencies, nonprofits, and Mississippi Valley State University)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Regional mobility-coordination network covering 21+ counties in NW Mississippi Delta; MDOT ConnectMS page describes it as 'a call center that provides connectivity between the systems' offering rides to employment, medical centers and other destinations. Own site states general 'families and communities' framing with no stated eligibility restriction (not ADA/senior-limited); phone-only reservation, no app/online booking found. Distinct from the state's only other inventoried MS system (Coast Transit Authority ADA Paratransit), which is a different region, operator, and eligibility model entirely.

Name: SMART
Ridership/Performance Notes: Listed by MDOT's ConnectMS as the regional mobility-coordination network for 13 counties in southwest Mississippi, providing non-emergency medical transportation, employment trips, and college shuttles. Corroborated independently by the Mississippi Public Transit Association resources page, which names the operator as S.M.A.R.T Regional Group. No independent operator website located across two research passes; eligibility criteria for general-public access not explicitly documented on either source.

Name: TRANS-CON (Transportation Connection)
Region/Service Area: Central Mississippi (Copiah, Hinds, Madison, Rankin, Simpson, Warren, Yazoo counties)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Regional mobility-coordination network for 7 counties in central Mississippi, listed on MDOT's ConnectMS program page. Independent search confirmed the operator as Jackson Medical Mall Foundation and the full county list. MDOT describes the service as offering vanpool/commuter employment trips, non-emergency medical transportation, and student transportation to local colleges/universities — these read as example trip purposes under a general-public rural transit umbrella (per ConnectMS's own general description of its network), not confirmed eligibility restrictions, but this distinction was not independently verified beyond the MDOT page. No independent TRANS-CON or Jackson Medical Mall Foundation page with fare/hours/fleet/vendor details was located.

Name: RideMon
Region/Service Area: Morgantown / Monongalia County (microtransit zone covering Mountain Heights and Grafton Road areas, connecting to Mountaineer Mall, Hornbeck Road Walmart, and Sabraton Goodwill)
Fare: $0.75 per passenger (same as fixed-route bus fare)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launched May 9, 2022 as a six-month pilot replacing coverage on low-performing Route 14 (Mt. Heights) and Route 15 (Grafton Road); originally booked via Uber's app under an Uber partnership, which ended June 2023 when the program switched to Spare's on-demand platform (current vendor). As of July 2026 the service had surpassed 15,000 total rides with roughly 600 rides/month, and RideMon ridership reportedly began outnumbering bus ridership in the same zone within about four months of launch.

Name: Ready Ride (PVTA)
Region/Service Area: Grant, Hardy, Hampshire, and Mineral Counties, WV (town-based zones in Petersburg, Moorefield, Romney, and Keyser)
Technology Vendor: Spare (inferred from Google Play package name for the 'Ride PVTA' app; not independently confirmed on PVTA's own site)
Fare: $2.00 per boarding (current site); one earlier PVTA social post cited $1.50 per boarding — discrepancy unresolved, may reflect a fare change over time
Service Hours: Monday-Friday (specific hours vary by zone; not fully published)
Ridership/Performance Notes: On-demand, no-fixed-route service that picks up multiple passengers within defined town zones; explicitly distinguished by PVTA from both fixed-route and NEMT/Medicaid transport. Petersburg zone launched July 1, 2019; Romney and Moorefield followed the same year; Keyser zone added around October 2019 (exact date unconfirmed). PVTA's separate Non-Emergency Medical Transport service (Medicaid-eligibility-restricted) is out of scope and not this row. PVTA also operates a distinct 'route deviation' fixed-route service, also out of scope.

Name: Here and There Transit (Demand Response)
Region/Service Area: Barbour County and portions of Taylor County, WV
Operator: Barbour County Senior Center, Inc. dba Here and There Transit Authority
Fare: Distance-based: $2.25 (up to 10 mi) to $3.00 (30+ mi within county); $1.00/extra stop; $8.00 out-of-county shopping trips; $16.00 Morgantown trips
Funding Source: FTA Section 5311 (rural formula, per WVDOT subrecipient status) plus local match; not itemized further
Fleet: 15 revenue vehicles per 2022 NTD data (mix of demand-response and fixed-route fleet, not broken out); wheelchair-lift-equipped
Ridership/Performance Notes: Door-to-door reservation-based service open to the general public throughout Barbour County (reserve travel from home to any in-county destination); distinct from the same operator's fixed 'Blue & Gray Loop' shuttle in Philippi (9 daily weekday trips, out of scope as fixed-schedule) and from its Non-Emergency Medical Transport program (Medicaid/sliding-scale, described separately from general demand-response on the rider's guide). Prior-day reservation required ('at least the day before'); same-day not offered per site language, consistent with Advance scheduling window.

Name: Aberdeen Ride Line
Region/Service Area: Aberdeen and within 2.5 miles of city limits
Ridership/Performance Notes: Open to the general public, all ages, no membership required, any trip purpose, per the city's own Ride Line page. Rides must be scheduled by 4:00 PM the prior business day and can be booked up to 1 week in advance.

Name: Brookings Area Transit Authority (BATA)
Operator: Brookings Area Transit Authority (private non-profit, SDDOT Section 5311 subrecipient)
Fare: $3.00/trip within Brookings city limits with advance reservation; $9.00/trip same-day within city limits
Ridership/Performance Notes: Door-to-door service the operator describes as 'not limited to who may use it; it is available for everyone' in Brookings County. Typically requires 1-day advance reservation; same-day service available at a higher fare.

Name: Brandon Transit
Fleet: Two 12-passenger buses, each with 2 wheelchair positions
Ridership/Performance Notes: Curb-to-curb service described by local coverage as 'available to all city residents.' Rides must be scheduled at least 1 day in advance. Owned by the City of Brandon and operated under contract by ROCS (Rural Office of Community Services), a separate multi-county provider also added in this sweep (see ROCS Transit).

Name: Community Transit of Watertown/Sisseton
Region/Service Area: 15-county service area in northeast SD centered on Watertown and Sisseton, including Clear Lake and Webster (Brown [excl. City of Aberdeen], Campbell, Clark, Codington, Day, Deuel, Edmunds, Faulk, Grant, Hamlin, parts of Lincoln, Marshall, McPherson, Roberts, and Spink counties)
Service Hours: Watertown office: Mon-Fri 6:00 AM-6:00 PM, Sat 6:00 AM-4:00 PM; Sisseton office: Mon-Fri 7:30 AM-4:00 PM
Ridership/Performance Notes: Nonprofit demand-response dial-a-ride; operator's own site states it serves 'seniors, veterans, students, employees' and general trip purposes with no stated eligibility restriction. Rides must be reserved at least 1 day ahead; fares vary by distance/trip location (amount not published).

Name: East Dakota Transit
Region/Service Area: Madison (3-mile radius) and Lake County, SD
Fleet: Wheelchair-lift-equipped bus(es); fleet size not specified
Ridership/Performance Notes: Operator states service is open to the public 'regardless of a person's age, handicap, race or sex'; ridership includes general public, school-age, and daycare riders. Rides scheduled by phone one day prior.

Name: Palace Transit
Ridership/Performance Notes: Curb-to-curb demand-response service the city's own site describes as open to 'anyone of any age' in Mitchell. Rides must be reserved by 4:00 PM the business day before travel.

Name: People's Transit
Fare: $3.50 general public; $2.50 seniors 60+ (donation) and youth under 18
Ridership/Performance Notes: Operator states its mission is to serve 'elderly, disabled, and general public.' Rides must be prescheduled; also offers non-emergency medical trips to other eastern SD cities (Sioux Falls, Brookings, Aberdeen, Mitchell, and others).

Name: River Cities Public Transit
Region/Service Area: Pierre/Fort Pierre and Hughes, Stanley, Hand, Hyde, Dewey, Ziebach, Haakon, East Pennington, North Jackson, Jones, Lyman, and Minnehaha counties, SD
Ridership/Performance Notes: Nonprofit serving 'individuals with disabilities, the elderly, low income as well as the general public' per operator's site. Offers same-day, on-demand ride requests as well as scheduled-ahead trips (discount for booking by 9pm the prior day). Also operates the Cheyenne River Sioux Tribal Transit contract, added separately in this sweep as Cheyenne River Sioux Transit.

Name: ROCS Transit
Region/Service Area: Multi-county south-central/southeastern SD, including Beresford-Alcester, Canton, Charles Mix County, Kingsbury County, Gregory County, Hartford, Miner County, Moody County, Parker, Parkston, Union County, Viborg-Centerville, Wessington Springs, Winner, and Brule-Lyman County
Operator: Rural Office of Community Services (ROCS), Inc.
Fare: $3 standard contribution in-town for riders 60+; other fares not published
Fleet: Wheelchair-accessible vehicles; fleet size not specified
Ridership/Performance Notes: Nonprofit dial-a-ride open to the general public; operator's site describes 'affordable and accessible transportation services' for medical, education, professional, social, shopping and personal needs, free for seniors 60+, Medicaid accepted. Rides scheduled 24 hours ahead. Distinct from Brandon Transit, a separate city-owned system ROCS manages under contract (added separately in this sweep).

Name: Southeast Public Transit (Yankton/Vermillion)
Region/Service Area: Yankton and Vermillion, SD (Yankton and Clay counties)
Operator: Yankton Transit, Inc., dba Southeast Public Transit
Service Hours: Yankton: Monday-Friday, 5:00 AM-5:00 PM; Vermillion: Monday-Friday, 7:30 AM-5:00 PM
Ridership/Performance Notes: Formed by the merger of the formerly separately-branded Yankton Transit and Vermillion Public Transit systems (both still listed individually as SDDOT Section 5311 rural subrecipients); open to the public with no stated eligibility restriction found. Yankton service requires booking the day before; Vermillion accepts same-day requests 'dependent upon availability' at a higher fare.

Name: Prairie Hills Transit
Region/Service Area: Black Hills region: Butte, Custer, Fall River, Lawrence, Meade, Perkins, and part of Pennington counties, SD (16 communities including Belle Fourche, Deadwood, Spearfish, and Sturgis)
Operator: West River Transit Authority, Inc., dba Prairie Hills Transit
Ridership/Performance Notes: Grew from a senior-only shuttle (Spearfish Senior Transportation, est. 1989) into a general-public county-wide door-to-door system; site states service is provided to 'students, elderly, individuals with disabilities, and the general public.' One business day's notice required.

Name: Cheyenne River Sioux Transit
Region/Service Area: Eagle Butte and surrounding communities, Cheyenne River Reservation, SD
Operator: River Cities Public Transit (operates under contract for the Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe)
Service Hours: Monday-Friday, 5:00 AM-6:00 PM; Saturday, 6:00 AM-3:00 PM
Ridership/Performance Notes: Open to the general public with no stated eligibility restriction per operator's site. Discounted fare for booking at least 1 day ahead; same-day service available based on driver availability at a higher rate. 23,481 annual unlinked passenger trips (2024 NTD data).

Name: Sisseton Wahpeton Oyate Transit
Region/Service Area: Lake Traverse Reservation, SD (Sisseton and surrounding communities)
Operator: Sisseton Wahpeton Oyate Department of Transportation
Fare: $3 round-trip (7 mi or less); $5 round-trip (over 7 mi); grocery trips within city limits free via store partnership
Service Hours: Monday-Friday, 6:00 AM-6:00 PM; office 8:00 AM-4:30 PM
Ridership/Performance Notes: Tribal DOT states its mission covers 'our traveling Oyate and General Public,' and is described in secondary sources as the sole source of public transportation on the Lake Traverse Reservation. Booking window (advance vs. same-day) not explicitly confirmed on the operator's own site; Advance is used here as a reasonable inference from phone-dispatch demand-response service consistent with peer SD tribal transit systems -- verify directly before relying on it.

Name: Rosebud Sioux Tribe Transit
Region/Service Area: Rosebud Reservation, Todd and Mellette counties, SD
Fleet: 14 revenue vehicles, 9 operated in maximum service (2022 NTD data)
Ridership/Performance Notes: NTD reports this as a demand-response public transit agency with 54,019 annual unlinked passenger trips (2022 data), confirming it is an operating public transit system rather than just a roads department. Eligibility ('who can ride') and booking/scheduling window could not be confirmed from the tribe's own site (transportation section not found / page unreachable); inclusion is inferred from NTD mode classification and consistency with peer general-public SD tribal transit systems (Cheyenne River, Sisseton-Wahpeton) rather than direct verification. HIGH PRIORITY: confirm eligibility language directly with the tribe before treating this row as settled in-scope.

Name: UTA On Demand
Region/Service Area: South Davis County, Salt Lake City Westside, Southern Salt Lake County, Tooele County, and West Provo/Orem (Wasatch Front); North Utah County zone (Eagle Mountain, Saratoga Springs, Lehi, American Fork, Pleasant Grove, Lindon, Highland, Cedar Hills, Alpine) launching Aug 17, 2026
Fare: $2.50 standard / $1.00 reduced fare; includes transfer to bus/TRAX/FrontRunner within 2 hours
Service Hours: Varies by zone; no Sunday service
Funding Source: Local, State (North Utah County zone sponsored by Utah County and UDOT; broader program funded through UTA's operating budget; federal FTA contribution plausible but not itemized on official materials)
Fleet: Via-operated vans (WAV); fleet size not specified; Tooele County zone switched to all-electric vehicles per a 2020s UTA announcement
Ridership/Performance Notes: 645,308 boardings in 2025 (13.6% year-over-year growth per UTA's 2025 rider-data report, published Jan 2026); over 2 million total riders since program launch. Originally piloted Nov 2019 in southern Salt Lake County (Bluffdale, Draper, Herriman, Riverton, South Jordan; ~65 sq mi, 7 TRAX/FrontRunner stations); has since expanded to 5 concurrent zones with a 6th (North Utah County) launching Aug 2026. Treated as a single multi-zone system, consistent with how High Valley Transit Micro's multiple microzones are handled in this database.

Name: Connect Pool (formerly CVTD POOL)
Region/Service Area: Providence, Millville, River Heights, Cliffside, and portions of Logan, Cache County
Operator: Connect Public Transit (Cache Valley Transit District)
Technology Vendor: Via (per current official site branding, "Connect On-Demand by Via"); Ecolane was reported as the vendor at the service's 2023 launch — see concerns.csv for this discrepancy
Service Hours: Monday-Friday 6:15 AM-8:45 PM; Saturday 9:45 AM-6:30 PM; no Sunday service
Fleet: 2 wheelchair-accessible vans (7-passenger capacity each) with bike racks, at 2023 launch; current fleet size not confirmed
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launched Feb 6, 2023 as "POOL" to cover four bus routes being removed or modified; initial expectation of 50-80 trips/day. Cache Valley Transit District rebranded as "Connect Public Transit" in 2024; the on-demand service continues under "Connect Pool"/"Connect On-Demand" branding with expansion plans noted on the operator's site.

Name: Moab Area Transit (MAT)
Region/Service Area: Moab and surrounding service area, Grand County
Service Hours: Peak season (Mar 16-Oct 15): 9 AM-9 PM daily; Off-peak (Oct 16-Mar 15): Monday-Friday 9 AM-5 PM, on-demand only (fixed Main Street route suspended off-peak)
Funding Source: State, Federal, Local ($10 million Utah Hotspot grant administered by UDOT; FTA; City of Moab; Grand County)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launched March 16, 2023 as Moab's first-ever public transit service; door-to-door on-demand microtransit supplements a fixed Main Street route. Only the on-demand/door-to-door component is in scope for this database; the fixed Main Street route is out of scope as fixed-route service.

Name: Fond du Lac Area Shared-Ride Taxi
Region/Service Area: City of Fond du Lac and Village of North Fond du Lac, WI (pickup/dropoff more than 1/4 mile from a fixed bus route)
Operator: Private taxi contractor under agreement with Fond du Lac Area Transit (contractor name not disclosed on source page)
Scheduling Window: Advance (phone reservation required by 4:30pm the weekday prior to travel; same-day requests accommodated based on driver availability)
Fare: $5.00 (ages 5-64); $4.00 with monthly pass; $3.00 for seniors 65+ with Medicare, individuals with disabilities, and children under 5 with adult
Service Hours: Monday-Friday 6:00am-6:30pm (no weekend service; limited holiday exceptions for Christmas Eve/Day and New Year's Eve/Day)
Funding Source: Not specified (Wisconsin's statewide Wis. Stat. 85.20 shared-ride taxi program is typically funded via WisDOT + FTA Section 5311/5307 + local match, but funding was not itemized on this source page)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Part of Wisconsin's statewide Wis. Stat. 85.20 shared-ride taxi program; supplements Fond du Lac Area Transit's fixed-route bus network by covering pickup/dropoff points more than 1/4 mile from a fixed route. Curb-to-curb, phone-dispatched, open to the general public with no eligibility-certification requirement found.

Name: Wisconsin Rapids Shared-Ride Taxi
Region/Service Area: City of Wisconsin Rapids and up to 5 miles outside city limits, WI
Operator: Running Inc. (private contractor) under agreement with City of Wisconsin Rapids
Technology Vendor: Not specified (Running Inc. operates its own online booking portal at runninginc.net; not a known third-party microtransit software vendor)
Scheduling Window: Advance (reservation required; exact advance-notice window not published on source page)
Funding Source: Local (City of Wisconsin Rapids transportation grant, per source page); state/federal funding plausible under WI's statewide shared-ride taxi program but not itemized on source page
Ridership/Performance Notes: Door-to-door shared-ride service; priority given to in-city passengers over the 5-mile extended zone. Multiple passengers may share a single trip via 'most appropriate route' dispatching; no guaranteed arrival time noted for mid-trip destination changes. General public, no eligibility restriction found on source page.

Name: Waupun Shared-Ride Taxi
Region/Service Area: City of Waupun, WI, plus trips outside the service area at a per-mile rate
Operator: Brown Cab Service, Inc. (contracted by City of Waupun)
Scheduling Window: Advance (phone reservation required; exact advance-notice window not published — source instructs riders to 'call to verify in advance')
Fare: $4.00 regular; $3.00 elderly/disabled/student; $9.75 agency; $2.75 additional passenger to same destination; $10.00 package delivery; $6.00 late night; $2.50/mile outside service area (2024 rates)
Service Hours: Mon-Thu 6am-6pm; Fri 6am-6pm and 9pm-2:30am; Sat 9am-2pm and 9pm-2:30am; closed Sunday (holiday exceptions apply; hours subject to change)
Funding Source: State, Federal (source states only 'state and federal funding'; consistent with the WI Wis. Stat. 85.20 shared-ride taxi program pattern but not itemized)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Source page explicitly states the service operates with 'no discrimination or restriction on trip purpose' — general public. Operated by Brown Cab Service under contract with the City of Waupun, part of the same multi-city Brown Cab shared-ride taxi network that also serves Medford, WI, and reportedly Edgerton, Fort Atkinson, Jefferson, Lake Mills, Monroe, Ripon, Sauk Prairie, and Whitewater, WI (those additional cities were identified via Brown Cab's own service-area list but not individually verified in this pass and are not yet added to the database).

Name: Medford Shared-Ride Taxi Service
Region/Service Area: City of Medford and a 5-mile radius, WI
Operator: Brown Cab Services, Inc. (contracted by City of Medford)
Scheduling Window: Advance (reservation required; exact advance-notice window not published on source page)
Fare: Not specified (source describes 'subsidized fare rides' and directs riders to Brown Cab's website for current rates)
Funding Source: City of Medford General Fund, State of Wisconsin DOT 85.20 Program, FTA Section 5311 Program, and rider fares (all confirmed on source page)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Demand-response service described as serving 'citizens in the community' (general-public framing; no eligibility-certification language found on source page). Operated by Brown Cab Services under contract with the City of Medford, part of the same multi-city Brown Cab shared-ride taxi network that also serves Waupun, WI.

Name: Viroqua-Westby Shared-Ride Taxi
Region/Service Area: City of Viroqua and City of Westby, WI
Operator: Passenger Transit, Inc. (contracted by City of Viroqua and City of Westby)
Scheduling Window: Advance (reservation required; exact advance-notice window not published)
Fare: $3.75 adult, $2.50 senior/disabled, $2.75 student, plus $7.00 Viroqua-Westby inter-city surcharge (current rates per City of Viroqua fare schedule; proposed increase to $4.00/$3.00/$3.00/$4.00 effective Jan 1, 2026)
Service Hours: Not specified (operator describes overall service as 'seven days per week, 365 days per year'; office hours Mon-Fri 8:00am-4:00pm; per-city daily service-hours not published)
Fleet: Wheelchair-accessible vehicles available per operator site; fleet size not specified
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public eligibility confirmed directly on operator Passenger Transit Inc.'s own site (passengertransit.net), which states no restriction to a specific eligible population and offers wheelchair-accessible vehicles. Passenger Transit also operates a third shared-ride taxi city, Watertown, WI, not independently verified or added in this pass.

Name: CARTS Dial-A-Ride
Region/Service Area: Central Kenai Peninsula: Soldotna, Kenai, Funny River, Kasilof, Nikiski, Sterling, and surrounding areas (13-zone service area)
Operator: Central Area Rural Transit System, Inc. (CARTS)
Fare: $25 one-way under 20 miles / $50 one-way 20+ miles; +$25 for an attendant; specific fare schedule per operator's Fares page
Service Hours: Monday-Saturday, 24 hours/day, except observed holidays (reservation office hours Mon-Sat 9am-5pm; rides must be scheduled by close of business the day before travel)
Funding Source: Federal (FTA 5311, FTA 5310), State, Local (Kenai Peninsula Borough)
Fleet: Not specified (historically 13-passenger vans plus wheelchair-accessible minivans; current fleet count not published)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Operator states 'CARTS provides public transportation for everyone' (open to general public, not ADA/senior-restricted). Nonprofit incorporated Jan 2000; service began operating later that year. Early operating history (2001) cited ~2,000 rides/month; current ridership not published.

Name: KATS Dial-A-Ride
Region/Service Area: City of Kodiak and specified areas outside city limits, Kodiak Island Borough
Operator: Senior Citizens of Kodiak, Inc. (program administrator); operated under contract by First Student Inc.
Booking Method(s): Phone (486-8308); registration required by phone or in person before first ride
Fare: $2.00 per one-way ride (pre-purchased e-pass or exact cash)
Service Hours: Monday-Friday 6:30 AM-6:30 PM; Saturday-Sunday 10:00 AM-3:00 PM
Ridership/Performance Notes: Operator states 'Everyone is eligible' to ride (explicitly open to general public, not ADA/senior-restricted). Rides must be scheduled a day or more in advance; cancellations require 2+ hours' notice; children under 10 cannot ride unaccompanied.

Name: GIFT On-Demand
Operator: City of Idaho Falls (Greater Idaho Falls Transit)
Funding Source: FTA grant ($4.2M) plus Idaho Transportation Department ($327,000); operating as a 2-year pilot
Ridership/Performance Notes: Replaced fixed-route service that ended in 2019. Open to general public with no age/disability eligibility restriction; rides can be booked same-day or up to 2 weeks in advance via the GIFT On-Demand app.

Name: VRT On-Demand (Nampa/Caldwell)
Region/Service Area: Nampa, Caldwell, and surrounding Canyon County
Fare: $1.50 single ride / $2.50 day pass (standard VRT fare)
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public on-demand microtransit zone booked via the "VRT Booking" app, rideVRT.org, or phone. Technology vendor inferred as possibly Via from the booking-page URL structure but not independently confirmed; recorded as Not specified per project convention.

Name: SPOT Boundary County Demand-Response
Region/Service Area: Boundary County (Bonners Ferry), with Thursday service to Sandpoint/Bonner County
Service Hours: Tue/Wed/Fri 9am-3pm (Boundary County); separate Thursday route to Sandpoint
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public curb-to-curb demand-response; site instructs riders to call at least a day in advance. Distinct from SPOT's separate fixed routes in Bonner County (Sandpoint/Dover/Ponderay/Kootenai, out of scope as fixed-route) and a separate ADA paratransit program (also out of scope).

Name: Pocatello Regional Transit Rural Door-to-Door
Region/Service Area: Bannock, Bear Lake, Bingham, Caribou, Franklin, Oneida, and Power counties (outside the Pocatello/Chubbuck urban area)
Fare: $2 one-way (general public); $2 suggested donation for riders 60+; $40/20-ride punch card
Ridership/Performance Notes: Operator's site states rural-area riders are eligible without ADA/age certification ("All residents living beyond Pocatello/Chubbuck but within PRT's service area... are eligible to ride"), distinct from PRT's separate in-town door-to-door service which IS restricted to ADA-certified riders and seniors 60+ (excluded from this database). Exact advance-notice window not confirmed from the source page.

Name: Lewiston Transit Dial-A-Ride
Ridership/Performance Notes: Source describes service as "available to the general public, no membership required," with ride priority given first to ADA-qualified riders, then seniors 60+, then general public -- the same priority-order pattern already used to justify including SMART Transit Dial-A-Ride (Twin Falls) in this database. Primary source page (PDF) could not be fully retrieved during this pass; most operational fields unconfirmed.

Name: Standing Rock Public Transit
Region/Service Area: Sioux, Morton, and Burleigh counties (ND) and Corson and Walworth counties (SD); serves 9 communities including Fort Yates
Ridership/Performance Notes: Described as "open to all"/general public by a secondary aggregator (Helpline Center) and by partner agency Bis-Man Transit's summary page, neither of which is the tribe's own primary source. The tribe's own program materials (a Sitting Bull College PDF) were image-based and unreadable via automated fetch, and the NTD agency profile page was blocked. Recommend a human verify general-public eligibility directly before treating this as fully confirmed.

Name: NW (Northwest) Dakota Public Transit
Region/Service Area: City limits of Williston and Watford City (Williams and McKenzie counties)
Operator: Williston Council for the Aging, dba NW Public Transit
Fare: $3 (general public); free for seniors and Williams County VA-card veterans
Service Hours: Williston Mon-Fri 6:30am-5:30pm; Watford City Mon-Fri 7:30am-4pm and 5pm-9pm
Ridership/Performance Notes: Operated by a senior-services nonprofit, but the eligibility language describes a general-public $3 fare service with senior/veteran fare waivers as add-ons rather than access gates. Reservations preferred 48+ hours in advance; airport trips require 1 week notice. Operator name ("Council for the Aging") suggests a possible senior focus -- worth a human sanity check against the SMART Transit / Lewiston precedent for priority-vs-restriction language.

Name: Wildrose Public Transportation
Region/Service Area: Northwest ND: Wildrose, Alamo, Zahl, Tioga, Ray, McGregor, Epping, Fortuna, Ambrose, Crosby, Noonan, Columbus, Lignite, Flaxton, Bowbells, Kenmare; longer routes to Williston, Minot, and Bismarck
Fleet: 3 vehicles: 10-passenger van, 12-passenger bus, and a minivan, all wheelchair lift/ramp equipped
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public service; seniors in Divide/Williams counties are sponsored via a separate Senior Citizen grant (a subsidy, not an access restriction). Also bills VA/Medicaid as one of several payer types for eligible riders, alongside general fare-paying public.

Name: MyBlue On-Demand Microtransit
Region/Service Area: Five zones: Espanola (15-mile radius of transit center), Taos (2-mile radius of Route 340), Pojoaque/Nambe, Edgewood, and La Cienega -- spanning Santa Fe, Rio Arriba, Taos, and Los Alamos counties
Fare: $1.00 per trip (most zones); free within the Pojoaque/Nambe zone; free for certified ADA paratransit riders and for military/veterans
Service Hours: Mon-Fri 6am-6pm (most zones); Edgewood 7:30am-5:30pm; La Cienega temporarily reduced to 6-7:30am and 3:30-4:30pm due to a stated staffing shortage as of Dec 2025
Fleet: Blue Bus / MyBlue microtransit vans; vehicle count not specified
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public zone-based on-demand microtransit requested via the "MyBlue North Central RTD" app or phone; no walk-ups permitted. Distinct from NCRTD's separate ADA-only paratransit program, which is excluded from this database as eligibility-restricted.

Name: RideKC Micro Transit (Johnson County)
Region/Service Area: Johnson County, KS — approx. 80-square-mile '499 Micro Transit' zone including Downtown Overland Park, Mission Transit Center, and KU Edwards Campus
Operator: Johnson County Transit (RideKC / Johnson County Government)
Fare: $5.00 for first 5 miles, $2.00 per additional mile; app or exact cash; Veterans Pass and JCCC Student Pass accepted
Fleet: Accessible vehicles available upon request; fleet size not specified
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public shared-ride on-demand service; riders must be 16+ or accompanied by an adult; no advance reservation required. Part of the multi-county RideKC On-Demand family of microtransit zones (see also Wyandotte County and Leavenworth rows).

Name: RideKC On-Demand (Wyandotte County / IRIS)
Region/Service Area: Wyandotte County / Kansas City, KS — multiple zones: Midtown KCK to Legends, Southwest Edwardsville, Northeast microtransit zone (added Feb. 3, 2025)
Operator: Unified Government of Wyandotte County and Kansas City, Kansas (UG Transportation)
Technology Vendor: Not specified (booked via 'IRIS' branded app/website; underlying platform vendor not confirmed)
Fare: $3.00 per person per ride; app or exact change; Veterans Pass or participating-school Student U-Pass accepted
Launch Year: Not specified (Northeast zone confirmed launched Feb. 3, 2025; Midtown/Legends and Edwardsville zones predate that)
Ridership/Performance Notes: UG's own announcement describes IRIS as 'an innovative new microtransit and paratransit service' — the general on-demand shared-ride zones (open to the public) are what's captured in this row; if UG operates a separate ADA-certified-only paratransit product under the same IRIS umbrella, that component is out of scope and not represented here. Part of the multi-county RideKC On-Demand family (see also Johnson County and Leavenworth rows).

Name: RideLV Micro Transit
Region/Service Area: City of Leavenworth, KS city limits, plus four addresses in Lansing, KS (Progress Drive; W. Eisenhower Rd/DaVita Dialysis; First Terrace)
Operator: The Guidance Center (contracted by City of Leavenworth)
Technology Vendor: Not specified (branded 'RideKC' app platform; specific white-label vendor not confirmed)
Fare: $2.00 per direction per rider, flat rate; cash requires exact change
Funding Source: KDOT Section 5311 grant ($266,655 operations; $219,545 vehicles) plus City of Leavenworth local match ($81,996 over three years from Countywide Sales Tax economic development allocation)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Open to general public; riders can schedule up to 7 days in advance via the app in addition to on-demand same-day booking; children under 18 must be accompanied by an adult. Launched April 2023.

Name: MOD Topeka (Metro On-Demand)
Region/Service Area: Designated southeast zone of Topeka, KS
Technology Vendor: Not specified (app store listing suggests Spare Labs platform; not independently confirmed on Topeka Metro's own site)
Fare: $2.00 one-way; exact cash, or debit/credit accepted since March 27, 2023
Service Hours: Monday–Friday 5:35 a.m.–6:40 p.m.; Saturday 8:15 a.m.–6:40 p.m.
Fleet: Fully accessible vehicles with lift/mobility device securements; count not specified
Ridership/Performance Notes: Curb-to-curb shared-ride microtransit within a defined southeast Topeka zone; open to general public; up to three children under 5 may ride with a paying adult; Wi-Fi equipped vehicles.

Name: OCCK OnDemand (Salina CityGo)
Technology Vendor: Transitioned software providers over time (TransLoc/Transit app integration circa 2022; new OnDemand-specific platform as of Dec. 15, 2025; specific current vendor name not confirmed)
Launch Year: Not specified (app-based booking dates to at least 2022; dedicated 'OnDemand' branding referenced from around Nov. 2024)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Curb-to-curb shared-ride service open to the general public within Salina city limits; distinct from OCCK's separately branded 14-county 'Regional Paratransit' program, which is out of scope for this database (eligibility-restricted).

Name: Reno County Area Transit (RCAT) Demand Response
Region/Service Area: Hutchinson and South Hutchinson, Reno County, KS
Fare: $2.00 per trip; exact cash or tickets required, no change given
Service Hours: Not specified (Monday–Saturday per operator; exact daily hours not published)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Door-to-door call-in service, distinct from Reno County's fixed-route and ADA paratransit programs; open to general public. Reservations may be made up to 7 days in advance, or next-day/same-day if availability permits; return trips must be scheduled and paid separately.

Name: CART (Cooperative Alliance for Regional Transportation)
Region/Service Area: Derry, Hampstead, Londonderry, and Salem, NH (curb-to-curb)
Fare: $2.00 per adult trip; $1.00 per child (ages 5–15); under 5 free; exact cash only
Service Hours: Derry: Mon–Fri 8:00 a.m.–7:30 p.m., Sat 9:30 a.m.–1:30 p.m.; Hampstead/Londonderry/Salem: Mon–Fri 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m.; reservation line Mon–Fri 6:30 a.m.–7:00 p.m., Sat 8:30 a.m.–6:00 p.m.
Ridership/Performance Notes: Curb-to-curb demand-response service; MTA's own service page states rides must be scheduled at least one business day (up to one week) in advance, with 24-hour cancellation notice required; no eligibility restriction language found — appears open to general public. MTA/CART also runs a separately branded Salem Shopper Shuttle with 3/4-mile route deviation on a fixed schedule (Mon/Wed/Fri) — that service is a fixed-route variant and is excluded per project precedent; only the curb-to-curb CART demand-response service is represented here.

Name: SCS Dial-A-Ride (Claremont)
Fare: Standard SCS Transportation Program fares apply (not separately itemized for Dial-A-Ride: roughly $1.50 within-town / $2.50 town-to-town / $10 eight-punch pass elsewhere on SCS's fare schedule)
Ridership/Performance Notes: SCS's own transportation page states the program 'is a shared ride service and is open to everyone.' Dial-A-Ride trips must be requested by noon the business day before the ride is needed. SCS also operates a separate 3/4-mile route-deviation service in Charlestown/Claremont/Newport, which is excluded per project precedent (fixed-route variant); only the Claremont Dial-A-Ride demand-response component is represented here.

Name: RTC OnDemand
Region/Service Area: Southwest Las Vegas Valley and West Henderson, Clark County, NV (approx. 32–33 square mile zone, expanded multiple times since launch)
Operator: Regional Transportation Commission of Southern Nevada (RTC)
Fare: $2.00 per ride for general riders; $3.00 for certified paratransit riders using the same on-demand fleet
