Funding Source: CARES Act / American Rescue Plan federal stimulus funds cited at launch (2021); current recurring funding not itemized
Fleet: Shared fleet serving both general on-demand and ADA-certified paratransit riders via RideCo's Microtransit Service Integrator; vehicle count not specified
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launched Sunday, August 8, 2021. Genuinely open to the general public (not restricted to paratransit-certified riders) — general riders are dropped at points of interest/transit stops while paratransit-certified riders in the same zone receive door-to-door service; ~50,000 total trips (fixed-route transfers, certified paratransit, and student riders combined) reported since inception as of a Jan. 2023 RTC committee presentation. This is distinct from RTC's separate ADA complementary paratransit program (RTC ACCESS), which remains out of scope for this database. rtcsnv.com blocks automated fetch (403); details sourced from RideCo's own case study/webinar, a public RTC committee PDF (via rtcsnv.civicweb.net), and Nevada Current news coverage.

Name: Lake Link (Nevada service area)
Region/Service Area: Douglas County, NV: Round Hill, Lower Kingsbury, Zephyr Cove, Stateline casino corridor (also serves South Lake Tahoe, CA — see existing CA row)
Operator: South Shore Transportation Management Association (South Shore TMA) / Tahoe Transportation District
Technology Vendor: Via (per ltva.org, June 2024); NOTE: existing CA-side row in this database lists vendor as 'Civic Mobility' — discrepancy not resolved, see concerns.csv
Service Hours: 7:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m. daily; extended to 11:00 p.m. Fri/Sat; 365 days/year
Launch Year: 2024 (per ltva.org; existing CA row lists 2022 — likely reflects an earlier CA-only pilot before the Nevada-side zone expansion, not independently reconciled)
Funding Source: Collaboration of public and private partnerships (specific sources not itemized)
Fleet: 9-12 passenger microtransit shuttles, wheelchair-accessible, bike/ski racks; count not specified
Ridership/Performance Notes: This is the SAME underlying bi-state Lake Link service already recorded in this database under CA (row 'Lake Link', South Lake Tahoe) — added here as a mirrored NV row per the established bi-state precedent (see 'Access AT' NH/VT) because Lake Link's service area demonstrably includes real Nevada communities (Round Hill, Zephyr Cove, Stateline, Douglas County), not just California. Open to both residents and visitors; children under 16 must be accompanied by an adult; only service animals permitted.

Name: CET Rural Dial-A-Ride
Region/Service Area: Prineville, La Pine, Madras, Redmond, Sisters, Warm Springs, plus a Deschutes River Woods pilot zone (Central Oregon)
Operator: Cascades East Transit (CET), operated by Central Oregon Intergovernmental Council (COIC)
Technology Vendor: Not specified (phone booking; Mobility by Ecolane app added Feb 2026)
Service Hours: Not specified (booking line M-F 7am-5pm; ride-service hours not confirmed)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Long-standing rural dial-a-ride program; March 30, 2026 regionwide expansion (not initial launch) added coverage; Deschutes River Woods pilot zone launched May 4, 2026. Distinguished by COIC/CET's own materials from Bend Dial-a-Ride and RIDE Assist, which are restricted to qualifying seniors/disabled riders (excluded, out of scope).

Name: Sunset Empire Transportation District Microtransit Pilot
Region/Service Area: Seaside and Cannon Beach (Clatsop County, North Coast), within the existing Route 20 service area
Funding Source: Providence Health Services grant ($50,000, secured Dec. 2024)
Fleet: 4 upfitted paratransit-style buses (shared with ADA paratransit fleet; no dedicated vehicles purchased)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launched June 1, 2025; general public confirmed eligible (fleet 'supports both ADA paratransit requirements and general public microtransit service'). Per SETD's own Feb 26, 2026 Board of Commissioners item, the program 'has ended and we are studying data to demonstrate value for future sustainability' (255 total trips, 26 unique riders, ~$52/ride operating cost over the pilot). Language is exploratory about relaunch, not a confirmed permanent shutdown; no evidence of relaunch found as of this research (July 2026).

Name: Basin Connect South
Region/Service Area: Keno, Worden, Falcon Heights, Lake of the Woods (Mon/Wed); Bly, Beatty, Bonanza, Merrill (Tue/Thu) — connecting into Klamath Falls
Fare: Free (riders receive a fixed-route Day Pass on arrival in Klamath Falls)
Service Hours: Not specified (varies seasonally; winter/summer timetables published separately)
Funding Source: State Transportation Improvement Fund (STIF) / payroll transit tax revenue
Ridership/Performance Notes: Riders must call a day or more ahead (e.g. 'call Friday for a ride on Monday,' 'call Monday for a ride on Tuesday'). Explicitly distinguished by Basin Transit's own site from 'Basin Lift,' its separate ADA/senior-eligibility paratransit product — clean general-public scope fit.

Name: Basin Connect North
Region/Service Area: Not specified — rural Klamath County north of Klamath Falls; specific towns not published on operator's site
Booking Method(s): Not specified (likely phone, 541-883-2877, shared dispatch line with Basin Connect South — not independently confirmed)
Fare: Free of charge for the general public (per operator's own site)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Sibling service to Basin Connect South; operator's site confirms general-public eligibility and free fare but does not publish service-area towns, hours, or booking details for the North product specifically. Included on confirmed scope fit despite thin operational data.

Name: SMART Flex
Region/Service Area: Zones in Dearborn, Troy/Clawson, Pontiac/Auburn Hills, Farmington/Farmington Hills, and the Hall Road corridor (Utica-New Baltimore) — Wayne, Oakland, and Macomb counties
Operator: SMART (Suburban Mobility Authority for Regional Transportation)
Fare: $2-$8 per ride by distance (+$2/extra rider up to 2); 50% discount for seniors/disabled
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launched March 2021 with 3 zones; expanded August 2021 and May 2022. Eligibility confirmed as general public ('anyone within the zones, including residents and workers'). Zone expansions since launch suggest sustained demand; no hard ridership figures found.

Name: CATA Rydz
Region/Service Area: Delta Township, downtown Lansing, MSU-to-airport corridor, plus late-night Lansing-Delta Township service
Service Hours: Mon-Fri 5:30am-8pm, Sat-Sun 9am-8pm (core zones); Airport/MSU 4am-1am daily; late-night 8pm-11:30pm daily
Funding Source: MDOT 2024 Service Initiatives grant ($1.664M) + MDOT 2024 Equitable Mobility Challenge grant ($1.687M)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launched November 12, 2024; late-night/airport trips require 2-hour prebooking. Lansing zone expanded August 18, 2025.

Name: BATA Link On-Demand
Region/Service Area: Grand Traverse and Leelanau Counties (Traverse City area and surrounding villages)
Fare: $6 full fare / $3 reduced (seniors, disabled, youth, military)
Service Hours: Weekdays 6am-10:30pm (limited after 7pm outside Traverse City); weekends 7am-7:30pm countywide, Traverse City until 10:30pm
Funding Source: FTA IMI grant ($276,499) + MDOT ($69,125) + Grand Traverse Regional Community Foundation/MI Health Endowment Fund ($50,000, NEMT+ add-on)
Fleet: Approx. 3-4 cutaway buses with wheelchair lifts at pilot outset (current fleet size not specified)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launched August 1, 2020. Confirmed 'open to all residents within the service area' per Shared-Use Mobility Center case study. About 80% of riders qualified for reduced fare during the 2020-21 pilot period. Vendor changed from TransLoc to Via at some point post-launch (not independently dated).

Name: TheRide FlexRide-East
Region/Service Area: Select areas of Ypsilanti Township, connecting to Ypsilanti Transit Center
Fare: $1.00 standard one-way; free for GoldRide seniors and A-Ride disabled ID holders; $0.50 K-12
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public eligibility confirmed on TheRide's own service page; launch date, funding, and fleet not found despite checking TheRide's news archive. Sibling service FlexRide-West was discontinued Jan 1, 2026 and replaced by a contracted operator in Pittsfield Township (not in scope, not added).

Name: MTA Genesee Connect
Region/Service Area: Hill Road corridor, Flint and Grand Blanc (Genesee County)
Technology Vendor: Via (inferred from Google Play package name com.ridewithvia.mtaflint; not independently confirmed on MTA's own site)
Fleet: Vehicles hold up to 3 ambulatory passengers or 1 wheelchair user
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launching July 2026 per MTA's own page, with more zones planned; too new for ridership data. Explicitly distinguished on MTA's site from 'Your Ride' (MTA's ADA/senior-restricted paratransit, out of scope) — Genesee Connect eligibility is 'anyone...within one of the zones.'

Name: BCGo
Operator: Battle Creek Transit (City of Battle Creek) — Calhoun County Coordinated Mobility Pilot
Fare: Mileage-based, quoted in-app at booking (+$3/extra passenger)
Service Hours: Mon-Fri 5am-7:30pm (current; originally also had Sat 9am-5pm at 2021 launch, which appears to have lapsed)
Funding Source: MDOT grant (Calhoun County Coordinated Mobility Pilot)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launched March 8, 2021 as a 12-month pilot; has continued operating since. General-public eligibility confirmed (only age-related boarding rules, no eligibility certification). Current hours differ from 2021 launch hours, suggesting a possible weekend-service reduction worth a follow-up check.

Name: Benzie Bus Dial-A-Ride
Operator: Benzie Bus / Benzie County Transportation Authority
Fare: $3.00 full / $1.50 reduced (60+, disabled, military/veteran, student); no-show penalty 2x fare
Ridership/Performance Notes: Eligibility page confirms general-public access with ADA/60+ riders prioritized but not exclusive — matches project's 'prioritizes but still general public' scope rule. Note: minimum 1-hour advance notice puts this at the boundary between Same-day and Advance; classified Same-day since booking can occur the same day the trip is needed.

Name: WexExpress
Region/Service Area: All of Wexford County; regional connections to Tustin and Traverse City
Ridership/Performance Notes: Operator's site states door-to-door service is 'available for everyone' (general public confirmed), but most operational fields (fare, hours, scheduling window, launch year, funding, fleet) could not be confirmed from the homepage alone.

Name: Charlevoix County Transit
Fare: Not specified (prepaid account system; fare schedule not published on rider page)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Lower-confidence scope call: no explicit eligibility-restriction language found, and no explicit general-public statement either — site describes service broadly as available 'throughout all of Charlevoix County' with no application/certification requirement mentioned. Included on that basis, consistent with other confirmed-general-public rural MI county systems in this batch, but flagged for human double-check.

Name: ROSCOTA
Region/Service Area: Roscommon County, with medical connections to neighboring/downstate counties
Technology Vendor: Not specified (uses a 'CTS Rider App' and dispatch software)
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public eligibility confirmed ('Roscommon county residents and visitors'). Classified Advance since 24-hour notice is the agency's own stated preference, though same-day is explicitly accommodated when possible — borderline call. Site notes current peak-time capacity constraints.

Name: MarqTran Door-to-Door
Region/Service Area: Greater Marquette, Ishpeming-Negaunee, Gwinn/Little Lake/K.I. Sawyer (Marquette County)
Fare: General public $2.60 starting, up to $5.60 max (mileage-based); reduced $1.30 (seniors/students/disabled/veterans); aides free
Service Hours: Varies by zone, e.g. Marquette 6:45am-8:30pm weekdays (see operator site for full table)
Funding Source: Not specified (FTA Section 5311 rural funding likely, unconfirmed)
Fleet: 5 buses total (2 Marquette, 2 Ishpeming-Negaunee, 1 Gwinn area), lift-equipped
Ridership/Performance Notes: Included because a separate general-public fare/booking tier exists alongside (not instead of) the operator's ADA-Paratransit tier — general public gets 1-day advance booking, working seniors 2-day, medical 3-day, ADA-Paratransit-eligible riders up to 7-day. Not certification-gated for general use.

Name: Black River Area Development (BRAD) Public Transit
Region/Service Area: City routes in Pocahontas, Walnut Ridge, Hoxie, Piggott, Corning; county routes into Clay, Lawrence, Randolph (plus stops in Greene, Craighead) counties
Fare: City routes $2/one-way or $10 unlimited-day pass; county routes $10/person
Service Hours: Varies by town, roughly Mon-Fri 8am-3pm (Corning Mon/Wed-Fri 9am-2pm, Piggott Tue only)
Launch Year: 1975 (program); current on-demand form not dated separately
Ridership/Performance Notes: Eligibility directly confirmed via operator site: 'Everyone! No income guidelines apply.' County routes require a 5-passenger minimum. 2019 ARDOT Public Transportation Directory recorded 25,667 annual rides (stale figure, not current).

Name: CADC/SCAT (South Central Arkansas Transit)
Region/Service Area: 19 south-central AR counties: Calhoun, Clark, Columbia, Dallas, Garland, Hempstead, Hot Spring, Howard, Little River, Lafayette, Lonoke, Miller, Montgomery, Nevada, Ouachita, Pike, Saline, Sevier, Union
Scheduling Window: Advance (minimum 24 hours; booking encouraged up to 3 weeks out)
Fare: Not specified (described as available 'at a reduced rate to any person, regardless of income')
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public eligibility confirmed on operator site. 24-hour advance minimum confirmed via a secondary source, not the primary page directly. 2019 ARDOT directory: 414,748 annual rides (stale figure).

Name: Mid-Delta Transit
Region/Service Area: Lee, Monroe, Phillips, Prairie counties (Helena-West Helena hub)
Scheduling Window: Advance (inferred from dial-a-ride model; exact notice period not published)
Fare: Not specified ('low-cost'; fare schedule available at community centers)
Launch Year: Not specified (parent organization dates to 1966; transit-specific launch not separately dated)
Funding Source: FTA Section 5311; also delivers Medicaid-funded rides via a separate SEAT partnership
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public eligibility confirmed on current site (no age/disability restriction stated). 2019 ARDOT directory: 96,758 annual rides (stale figure).

Name: North Arkansas Transportation Service (NATS)
Region/Service Area: Baxter, Boone, Carroll, Fulton, Izard, Madison, Marion, Newton, Searcy counties (Harrison/Mountain Home hub)
Fare: Not specified (approx. $3.00 base per 2019 data; current rate not confirmed)
Fleet: 64 vans/small buses plus support vehicles per NWAEDD site (undated; likely covers combined commuter + demand-response fleet)
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public eligibility directly confirmed on operator's own site ('no restrictions such as age etc.'). 2019 ARDOT directory: 124,843 annual rides (stale figure).

Name: North East Arkansas Transportation (NEAT)
Region/Service Area: Craighead, Cross, Crittenden, Greene, Jackson, Mississippi, Poinsett, St. Francis, Woodruff counties (Jonesboro hub)
Scheduling Window: Advance (48-hour notice per 2019 ARDOT directory; current site confirms rides 'must be scheduled in advance' without restating the hour count)
Fare: Not specified (approx. $8.00 base per 2019 data; current rate not confirmed)
Ridership/Performance Notes: 'No income guidelines' curb-to-curb general-public service directly stated in 2019 ARDOT directory text; current site reconfirms general framing but is thinner on specifics. 2019 directory: 7,484 annual rides (stale, notably low).

Name: Southeast Arkansas Transportation (SEAT)
Region/Service Area: Full service in Arkansas, Ashley, Bradley, Chicot, Cleveland, Desha, Drew, Grant, Jefferson, Lincoln counties; limited service in Calhoun, Dallas, Lee, Lonoke, Monroe, Phillips, Prairie, Union counties (Pine Bluff hub)
Operator: Area Agency on Aging of Southeast Arkansas (AAASEA)
Funding Source: FTA Section 5311; also Medicaid NEMT contracts as a separate revenue stream
Fleet: 113 vans per 2019 directory (103 wheelchair-accessible) — likely stale
Ridership/Performance Notes: Eligibility directly confirmed on current site: 'all ages without regard to...handicap...or disability' — general public, not certification-gated, despite Medicaid NEMT being one revenue stream. Named 2008 CTAA Rural Community Transportation System of the Year. 2019 directory: 227,868 annual rides (stale figure).

Name: Western Transit System (WTS)
Region/Service Area: Conway, Crawford, Franklin, Johnson, Logan, Perry, Polk, Pope, Scott, Sebastian, Yell counties
Operator: Area Agency on Aging of Western Arkansas
Scheduling Window: Advance (48 business hours required; bookable up to 1 month ahead)
Fare: Not specified on current site (2019 data: $6.00 round trip)
Fleet: Ambulatory and wheelchair-accessible vans (current count not specified; 2019 directory: 10 vehicles)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Directly confirmed on current site as 'a transportation program for all residents who need rides' despite parent organization being an Area Agency on Aging — included on that explicit general-public language, mirroring the NATS precedent in this same batch. 2019 directory: 2,666 annual rides (notably low, likely stale).

Name: NICE Mini
Region/Service Area: Nassau County - South Shore zone (Merrick-Lynbrook corridor to Hicksville LIRR) and Syosset/Plainview/Woodbury/Muttontown/East Norwich zone
Operator: Nassau Inter-County Express (NICE); operated under contract by Transdev
Fare: $3.00 regular / $1.50 reduced; $3.50 single-ride e-ticket by card
Service Hours: Begins 6:00am daily; end time not published on official site
Ridership/Performance Notes: Two zones as of 2024 (South Shore launched June 2022; Syosset zone added Summer 2024). NICE has stated plans for up to 4 additional Mini zones over the following 3 years.

Name: Suffolk Transit On-Demand
Region/Service Area: Southampton zone (Stony Brook Southampton campus/Shinnecock Hills to South Ferry/North Haven incl. Sag Harbor) and East Hampton zone (East Hampton LIRR to Montauk Point incl. Springs/Amagansett)
Operator: Suffolk County Transit; operated by Hampton Jitney
Technology Vendor: Via Mobility LLC (per county press coverage; not independently confirmed on operator's own site)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Southampton zone launched 2021; East Hampton zone added later (partnership announcement referenced an April 28 launch; year not independently confirmed, likely 2024). Operator's own site (sctbus.org) returned 403 to automated fetch; details corroborated via county legislature and town-government pages instead.

Name: Circuit New Rochelle (CircuitNR)
Region/Service Area: Downtown New Rochelle plus expanded southern/eastern zones (YMCA on Weyman Ave, Montefiore on Cedar St)
Operator: Circuit, in partnership with City of New Rochelle
Funding Source: Municipal (City of New Rochelle) + sponsor/advertiser partnerships
Fleet: 100% electric vans/sedans/low-speed neighborhood vehicles; count not specified
Ridership/Performance Notes: Not specified

Name: Circuit Rockaways (Rockaway Rides)
Region/Service Area: Rockaway Peninsula - 116th St/Far Rockaway LIRR corridor, beach, Rockaway Hotel, transit hubs
Fare: Free per official site; one Feb 2026 news article referenced a possible $2.50 fare - discrepancy unresolved
Funding Source: $7M grant from NYSERDA (New York Clean Transportation Prizes Program), supported by LIPA
Ridership/Performance Notes: Feb 2026 news coverage described the pilot as 'nearing its end' as grant funds are exhausted, with Circuit/community seeking extension funding; current operating status as of this research (July 2026) could not be independently verified.

Name: Circuit Brentwood
Region/Service Area: Brentwood - Hauppauge Industrial Area, Suffolk County Community College, LIRR
Ridership/Performance Notes: Not specified

Name: Circuit Southampton
Region/Service Area: Southampton village - LIRR, beach, Main Street
Ridership/Performance Notes: Geographically overlaps with Suffolk Transit On-Demand's Southampton zone but is a separately operated, differently funded service (free flag-down/app vs. $2.25 fare app-booked service).

Name: Circuit East Hampton
Region/Service Area: East Hampton village - LIRR station, Jitney stop, Main Street, Main Beach
Ridership/Performance Notes: Overlaps geographically with Suffolk Transit On-Demand's East Hampton zone; separately operated service.

Name: Circuit Montauk
Region/Service Area: Montauk - Bayfront Park, The Plaza, Jitney stop, beachside hotels
Ridership/Performance Notes: Not specified

Name: Buffalo All Access
Region/Service Area: Buffalo Niagara Medical Campus and surrounding neighborhoods
Operator: Niagara Frontier Transportation Authority (NFTA), in partnership with Buffalo Niagara Medical Campus (BNMC) and University at Buffalo
Ridership/Performance Notes: Community shuttle component is operating; a companion autonomous 'All Access Loop' shuttle was announced but not yet confirmed launched as of research date. Service is centered on the medical campus district but framed by the operator as open to the general public ('designed so everyone can travel with confidence'), not restricted to campus affiliates - flagged for a human eligibility double-check given the campus-adjacent framing.

Name: RTS On Demand
Region/Service Area: Seven-county Rochester region: Genesee, Livingston, Ontario, Orleans, Seneca, Wayne, and Wyoming counties (7 zones, each connecting to RTS Connect bus stops)
Operator: Rochester Genesee Regional Transportation Authority (RGRTA) / RTS
Technology Vendor: Conflicting sources: myrts.com branding/URL pattern suggests Via; a Feb 2025 The Routing Company press release describes the same 7-county rollout as powered by TRC's Pingo platform with 132 vehicles - not resolved, flagged as a discrepancy
Service Hours: Weekday service; a 2026 service-change notice eliminated weekend and after-8pm weekday RTS On Demand service effective Sept 7, 2026, implying broader hours previously existed in at least some zones
Fleet: 132 vehicles across the 7-zone service area per Feb 2025 press release, not independently confirmed on operator's own site
Ridership/Performance Notes: Zones phased in starting early 2025 (Seneca, Genesee, Orleans, Ontario, Wyoming first; Wayne and Livingston in spring 2025). General public eligibility confirmed on myrts.com.

Name: Centro MOVE
Operator: Central New York Regional Transportation Authority (Centro)
Fleet: Wheelchair-accessible vehicles available on request; count not specified
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launched March 5, 2024 in Rome alongside a consolidated 3-route fixed-network redesign. A Nov 2025 news article referenced a 'new on-demand service' as part of a broader Centro system redesign in Syracuse/Onondaga County, but no Syracuse-specific on-demand zone could be confirmed as launched - worth a follow-up check.

Name: Franklin County Public Transportation (Southern Zone Demand-Response)
Region/Service Area: Southern Franklin County - Saranac Lake, Tupper Lake (zone-based, curb-to-curb)
Funding Source: County, State (NYSDOT 5311 rural formula program plausible but not explicitly confirmed on source page)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Operator's own site states 'Anyone Can Ride' - explicitly general public, with a senior/disabled/student fare discount, not an access gate. Distinct from Franklin County's Northern routes (Malone, Chateaugay, Burke, Fort Covington), which are fixed-route with route deviation and were excluded here as a fixed-route variant, not standalone demand-response.

Name: Putnam On-Demand
Region/Service Area: Putnam County (replaced former PART Route 3; county seat Carmel)
Operator: Putnam County Dept. of Planning Development & Transportation; operated by Via
Fare: $2.50 standard; $1.25 reduced (senior/student/ADA); $0.75/$0.25 transfer to/from PART fixed route
Fleet: Wheelchair-accessible vehicles, ADA-trained drivers; count not specified
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launched May 12, 2025. Operator's page confirms service is available to the general public and also serves paratransit-eligible riders with accessible vehicles (not gated to ADA/senior certification). Funded via urbanized-area 5307 rather than rural 5311, despite Putnam's semi-rural/exurban character - flagged as a categorization edge case.

Name: Dutchess County Dial-A-Ride & Flex
Region/Service Area: Dial-A-Ride: Towns of East Fishkill, Fishkill, Hyde Park, Poughkeepsie, Wappinger, and City of Poughkeepsie. Flex: all Dutchess County municipalities.
Fare: Dial-A-Ride: $3.50 one-way ($1.00 reduced for seniors 60+/veterans/disabled); Flex: $5.00 same-town / $6.00 different-town one-way; same-day Dial-A-Ride within City of Poughkeepsie available for $7.00 space-available
Ridership/Performance Notes: Both programs open to general public residents (Dial-A-Ride: residents of 6 participating municipalities; Flex: all county residents); reduced fare for seniors/veterans/disabled is a discount, not an eligibility gate. Reservations required 3-30 days in advance.

Name: Transit Orange Dial-A-Ride Network
Region/Service Area: Nine Orange County municipalities: Goshen, Chester, Highlands, Monroe, Montgomery, Warwick, Wallkill, Newburgh (town), Crawford, Kiryas Joel, and Port Jervis/Deerpark (town-level programs coordinated under the county Transit Orange umbrella)
Operator: Orange County Transit / individual town transportation departments (each town operates its own dial-a-ride under the shared Transit Orange umbrella)
Fare: Varies by town, $0.50-$6.00 per trip; most areas offer discounted senior/youth fares of $0.50-$1.00
Service Hours: Generally 6:00am-5:00pm weekdays; a few towns (Monroe, Wallkill, Warwick) offer Saturday service
Ridership/Performance Notes: Curb-to-curb, open to the public per the operator's own site; reservations required at least 24 hours in advance (some towns require up to 1 week, e.g. Chester at $4.00 general/$2.00 senior-disabled). Each town runs an independently operated program under the shared Transit Orange brand - treated here as one aggregate system entry rather than 9 separate rows; Goshen/Chester, Monroe, and Port Jervis were spot-verified, other towns taken from the regional overview page only.

Name: Move Sullivan
Region/Service Area: Sullivan County (Highland and Delaware runs confirmed; county-wide per operator page)
Operator: Sullivan County Division of Community Resources
Service Hours: Booking line open 8:00am-3:00pm; operating hours not published
Ridership/Performance Notes: Confirmed general-public eligibility (not restricted to seniors/disabled) on operator's own transportation page. Reservations required at least 24 hours before trip via phone (845-807-0180). Operational hours and exact service-area boundary not published on the source page - worth a follow-up call to the department.

Name: LANtaFlex
Region/Service Area: Lehigh Valley flex zones: 501 Macungie, 502 Slate Belt, 503 Slatington/Walnutport, 504 Coplay/Egypt Airport, 505 Coopersburg, 506 Bath-Hanoverville-Nazareth, 507 West/South Easton (Lehigh and Northampton counties)
Fare: Standard LANTA fares (passes/transfers accepted; cash one-way fares accepted onboard)
Service Hours: Reservation line Mon-Fri 8:00am-4:00pm; standing reservations available for daily commuters
Fleet: Small transit vans, approx. 16-passenger capacity, shared-ride service
Ridership/Performance Notes: One of PennDOT's 6 statewide microtransit case-study systems (2024 report); operates in defined flex zones (largest over 25 sq mi) with transfer points to fixed LANTA routes, not a route-deviation service; reservations required at least 2 hours ahead, up to 14 days in advance; shares Ecolane software/reporting with LANTA's ADA paratransit and shared-ride service, so some agency-reported data combines microtransit and shared-ride trips.

Name: BCTA Connect
Region/Service Area: Beaver County, PA (in-county); out-of-county destination service added Feb 2026
Fare: $4.00 per passenger (trips up to 10 miles); $5.00 per passenger (trips over 10 miles); children 50% discount when riding with a paying adult
Ridership/Performance Notes: Curb-to-curb on-demand service; app scheduling opened Jan 6 2025; an out-of-county destination expansion went live Feb 2, 2026; a public hearing on further proposed Connect service changes was posted July 22, 2026; local news (not independently accessed) referenced planned expansion of Connect service into Allegheny and Butler counties.

Name: Goose Creek Transit
Fare: $4.00 general public / $2.50 seniors within Sheridan; $10.00 general public / $7.00 seniors outside city
Ridership/Performance Notes: Dial-a-ride serving downtown Sheridan, Northern Wyoming Community College, Dayton, Ranchester, and Sheridan Memorial Hospital; operated by Sheridan Senior Center but open to all riders — separate general-public and senior fare tiers confirm non-restricted eligibility; reservations must be made a day ahead.

Name: Buffalo Area Transit System (BATS)
Region/Service Area: Buffalo & Johnson County, WY; weekly regional trips to Sheridan and Gillette; Kaycee local service
Fare: $1.00 local in-town; $2.00 outside town limits; regional (Sheridan/Gillette) fares not specified
Service Hours: In-town Mon-Fri 8:00am-5:00pm (office Mon-Fri 7:00am-5:00pm); regional trips to Sheridan Mon/Wed/Fri and Gillette Tue/Thu
Fleet: 4 buses (3 serving Buffalo, 1 serving regional routes); wheelchair-accessible vehicles available
Ridership/Performance Notes: Dial-a-ride/on-demand service requiring new rider registration; requests 24-hour advance booking (2-hour minimum if unavoidable); 1-hour cancellation notice required; 3-strikes no-show policy (30-day suspension). New Kaycee local service recently added.

Name: STAR Transit Door-to-Door
Region/Service Area: Rock Springs & Green River, Sweetwater County, WY (other county areas with advance notice)
Operator: Sweetwater County Transit Authority Resource (STAR Transit)
Fare: $2.00 adults/youth over 10; free for seniors 60+; free for up to 2 children under 10 with adult ($1.00 each additional child); $75/month pass
Service Hours: Mon-Fri 7:00am-5:00pm (trips must be scheduled by 5:00pm the day before); closed weekends and holidays
Ridership/Performance Notes: Curb/door pickup and dropoff (riders at apartment/trailer complexes may be asked to board at a designated central point); requires reservations at least 24 hours in advance. STAR also runs a separate fixed 'Stop-to-Stop' route service (Blue/Red Line, Green River Shuttle) not counted as a distinct system here.

Name: SafeRide (Laramie)
Region/Service Area: City of Laramie, WY (within city limits)
Operator: University of Wyoming Transportation & Parking Services
Ridership/Performance Notes: Curb-to-curb, on-demand; operator's own site states 'SafeRide is open to the public, so anyone can ride!' (children must be accompanied by a parent/guardian); wheelchair accessible with advance notice; distinct from UW's separate fixed-route 'Roundup' bus service.

Name: Campbell County Dial-a-Ride
Region/Service Area: Gillette & Campbell County, WY (within city limits and countywide with notice)
Fare: Within Gillette: $3.00 (senior/veteran/disabled) or $5.00 (general public) per stop; outside city/within county: $5.00 or $8.00 per stop; punch cards $60 (eligible groups) or $100 (general public) for 20 rides
Funding Source: Federal Transit Administration and State Public Transit programs, administered through WYDOT
Ridership/Performance Notes: Door-to-door service explicitly open to the general public at a higher fare tier alongside a senior/veteran/disabled discount tier; first-time riders must call to register. Distinct from the separate fixed-route Campbell County Public Transportation bus service in Gillette/Wright, not counted here.

Name: Cody Senior Center Transportation
Region/Service Area: Cody and up to 10 miles outside city limits, Park County, WY
Ridership/Performance Notes: Operator's own site describes service as available to 'seniors and general public' with a differentiated per-stop fare for each; requires minimum 24-hour advance notice.

Name: Gopher
Region/Service Area: Washington County, VT plus three neighboring northern Orange County towns (Barre-Montpelier area)
Fare: Tiered: subsidized rides for eligible Vermonters, market-rate taxi-like fares, and contracted corporate/institutional rates; exact dollar amounts not published
Ridership/Performance Notes: Nonprofit 501(c)(3) launched as "Community Rides Vermont," branded Gopher / Gopher-It Rideshare Program. Site states no explicit general-public restriction, and optimal booking window is 2-7 days ahead, but same-day/last-minute requests are explicitly accommodated when possible - recorded as Flexible scheduling window. Also operates as a subcontractor for Medicaid NEMT and Older Adults & People with Disabilities programs; those restricted programs are out of scope, only the general-public rideshare service is represented here.

Name: Mountain Town Connector
Region/Service Area: 14 towns in the greater Londonderry/southern Vermont mountain area, incl. Andover, Chester, Chester Depot, Jamaica, Windham, Winhall
Funding Source: Not specified (originated via BDCC Community Facilities Technical Assistance and Training Program on behalf of USDA Rural Development)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Nonprofit resource-center program; own materials describe "no age or income criteria to catch a ride" and "on-demand scheduling, flexible fixed routes, and group transportation trips." Medical-related rides are prioritized but not exclusive. Door-through-door service; drivers may accompany riders into appointments. Single-van fleet limits capacity/scale.

Name: MyRide by TVT (Middlebury)
Region/Service Area: Middlebury, VT (Addison County; mapped zone, exact boundary shown only on operator map)
Fleet: Vehicles up to 8 passengers, wheelchair-lift accessible, service animals accommodated (shared TVT MyRide fleet spec, per existing Montpelier MyRide row)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Replaced the prior EZ Trip service in Middlebury as of July 15, 2026 (same relaunch date as TVT's Montpelier MyRide zone, already in this CSV as a separate row); bookable 1 hour to 21 days in advance per TVT's own site (differs from Montpelier zone's 15-minute-to-30-day window) with Arrive By/Depart By options. Distinct mapped zone from Montpelier; not a duplicate of the existing MyRide by TVT (Montpelier) row.

Name: WinReady
Operator: City of Winchester (WinTran) / Via Transportation, Inc.
Fare: Free (as of research date; funded in part by temporary ARPA/federal support per city transit funding page)
Service Hours: Not specified (typical pickup ~30 min after request)
Funding Source: Federal (FTA, ~50% of Winchester Transit funding), State (DRPT, ~16%), Local (City General Fund, ~34%)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launched March 25, 2024 as a free, publicly operated point-to-point rideshare service covering the entire City of Winchester; complements the WinTran fixed-route system. Via's ninth tech-enabled transit deployment in Virginia per RideWithVia coverage.

Name: MetroFLX
Region/Service Area: Cities of Roanoke and Salem, and Town of Vinton, VA
Technology Vendor: Not specified (booked via Valley Metro's VMGO app; underlying platform vendor not identified)
Fare: Same as regular Valley Metro bus fare; cash only as of research date
Service Hours: Mon-Sat 8:45pm-12:45am (starts when fixed-route service ends), Sun 9:00am-6:00pm
Fleet: RADAR vans (wheelchair-lift equipped); fleet size not specified
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launched Jan 22, 2024 to extend service after fixed-route buses stop running and to cover Sunday service; door-to-door within the Roanoke/Salem/Vinton tri-city area. Celebrated 2-year anniversary Jan 2026.

Name: GLTC Flex
Region/Service Area: Lynchburg, VA (designated zone incl. Graves Mill Rd, Enterprise Dr, Timberlake Rd, airport area)
Fare: Same as standard GLTC bus fare; discounted fares available for eligible riders
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launched Aug 2, 2024 (ribbon-cutting); provides customized point-to-point trips within a designated Lynchburg zone as an alternative to fixed-route buses. Open to the general public.

Name: HRT OnDemand
Region/Service Area: Zones in Virginia Beach (~15 sq mi), Newport News (~20 sq mi), Chesapeake (~11.3 sq mi), and Hampton (~5.9 sq mi)
Fare: $2/ride; free for qualified paratransit riders and Student Freedom Pass holders; children under 17 free with paying adult
Ridership/Performance Notes: Original Newport News/Virginia Beach pilot ran July 2022-Feb 2023 (26,258 and 13,037 ride requests respectively); relaunched Oct 2024 and expanded to Chesapeake and Hampton Jan 2025. First/last-mile connector to HRT fixed-route bus and light rail. Pilot funding runs through Oct 2026 per one source.

Name: LC Transit On Demand
Region/Service Area: Leesburg (~5-6 sq mi zone) and Sterling (~14 sq mi zone), Loudoun County, VA
Booking Method(s): LC Transit On Demand app, Web (book.lct.rideco.com), Phone (571-258-3464)
Service Hours: Leesburg: Mon-Fri 7am-7pm (weekend service added Jul 5, 2026); Sterling: Mon-Fri 6am-8pm, weekends 8am-10pm
Funding Source: State (DRPT grant; also cites a Low-No Transit Enhancement Grant)
Fleet: Minivans and 6-passenger buses (green Transit On Demand decals)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Leesburg pilot launched 2025 and "exceeded expectations," prompting expansion to Sterling; Leesburg and Sterling are independent zones (trips cannot cross zones; use Route 70 bus to connect). Open to the general public.

Name: Arlington Microtransit (MICRO)
Region/Service Area: Northwest Arlington (two zones: Arlington North and Arlington South), bounded by North Glebe Rd, Langston Blvd, and the county line
Fare: $4.50 standard; $2.25 for seniors, persons with disabilities, K-12 students, and Metrorail connections; additional passengers $2.25 each; children under 5 free
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launched Apr 13, 2026 as a stopgap replacing low-ridership fixed-route ART service in northwest Arlington; virtual bus-stop pickup/dropoff model connecting to East Falls Church Metro, Ballston-MU Metro, Virginia Hospital Center, and Madison Community Center. Riders must be 13+ unless with a guardian.

Name: Union County On-Demand Micro-Transit Pilot
Region/Service Area: 1.5-mile radius zone centered on Route 28 & South Avenue (County Route 610), Union County, NJ (~35,000 residents)
Operator: Union County (River North Transit, LLC / Via)
Funding Source: Local (Union County contract with Via); specific grant/funding line not itemized in county announcement
Ridership/Performance Notes: One-year pilot approved by the Union County Board of County Commissioners; launching Summer 2026 near the Westfield/Scotch Plains/Fanwood area to address employment, healthcare, shopping, and first/last-mile transit gaps. ADA-compliant, open to all riders.

Name: GOTrenton!
Region/Service Area: City of Trenton, NJ and surrounding areas
Operator: Isles, Inc. (with NJ Dept. of Environmental Protection support)
Funding Source: State (NJ Dept. of Environmental Protection); Private/Nonprofit (Isles, Inc.)
Fleet: Electric shuttles/vans, including Kia Niro EVs
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launched Oct 2023; free/emission-free electric rideshare for the city of Trenton, expanded April 2025; surpassed 100,000 riders per Trenton Journal coverage.

Name: ARTS (Aroostook Regional Transportation System)
Region/Service Area: Aroostook County, ME, plus Danforth (Washington County) and Patten (Penobscot County)
Fare: Free for low-income residents; other riders pay by check or cash (amount not specified)
Service Hours: Office hours Mon-Fri 6:00am-4:30pm; ride service hours not specified
Fleet: Vehicles equipped with wheelchair lifts and car seats; fleet size not specified
Ridership/Performance Notes: Door-to-door demand-response service open to the general public (confirmed via multiple sources describing service to "the general public, individuals with disabilities, and the elderly"), not limited to eligibility-certified riders. Requires at least 1 business day advance notice; a few days recommended to guarantee availability.

Name: RIDE Hancock
Region/Service Area: Hancock County, IN (Greenfield and surrounding areas; limited out-of-county trips at premium rates)
Fare: $4.00 per stop (general public); donation-based for seniors 60+ on essential trips (medical, grocery); $4/stop for seniors on non-essential trips; bulk ride vouchers available
Funding Source: Not specified (FTA Section 5307 pass-through from IndyGo referenced by a secondary source, not confirmed on operator site)
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public shared-van dial-a-ride operated by the nonprofit Hancock County Senior Services; open to all riders, first-come first-served, call as early as possible to reserve. Limited out-of-county service available at premium rates.

Name: Marshall County Rural Transit (MCPT)
Region/Service Area: Marshall County, IN (Plymouth and county-wide); out-of-county trips within a 2-hour radius including South Bend/Mishawaka, Fort Wayne, and Indianapolis
Fare: $2.50 per boarding for in-town Plymouth service; out-of-town medical trips for riders 60+ are donation-based (Title III Older Americans Act funding)
Service Hours: Mon-Fri 6:00 AM-6:00 PM (last call for in-town Plymouth service 5:00 PM)
Funding Source: United Way of Marshall County, Area 2 Agency on Aging, FTA, INDOT
Ridership/Performance Notes: Demand-response, curb-to-curb service explicitly marketed as open to the general public ('MCPT is public transportation so anyone can ride!'); same-day phone dispatch, no fixed schedule -- classified as Microtransit per project convention despite phone-only (no app) booking. Also provides separate Medicaid-funded trips for eligible riders.

Name: Area 10 Agency on Aging Rural Transit
Region/Service Area: Monroe, Owen, Lawrence, and Putnam counties, IN (plus a deviated fixed-route in Greencastle)
Fare: $3.00 one-way / $6.00 round-trip within one county; $6.00 one-way / $12.00 round-trip crossing two counties
Service Hours: Mon-Fri 6:00 AM-6:00 PM (closed holidays); reservation lines Mon-Fri 8:30 AM-4:30 PM
Funding Source: Not specified (federally funded program per operator, exact sources not itemized)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Door-to-door demand-response open to any resident of the four-county service area ('anyone can ride'), though the agency's primary focus is seniors/disabled/caregivers. 3-5 day advance notice required; first-come first-served scheduling. Children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult.

Name: TRAM (The Ride Around Madison)
Region/Service Area: Rural Madison County, IN (trips must originate or end outside the Anderson urbanized area)
Fare: $4.00 per trip (under 60) or $33/month unlimited; $2.50 per trip (60+) or $25/month unlimited
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public demand-response door-to-door service for rural Madison County residents; distinct from Anderson's in-city CATS fixed routes/paratransit. At least 24 hours advance notice required; payment via voucher purchased from the driver at pickup.

Name: Catch-A-Ride (Lifetime Resources)
Region/Service Area: Ripley, Jefferson, Dearborn, Ohio, Switzerland, and Decatur counties, IN (southeast Indiana)
Fare: $3.00 base (0-5 miles) plus $0.25/additional mile; reduced $2.00 base fare for seniors 60+, children up to 16, and persons with permanent disabilities; $4.50 base subscription option; group rates available
Service Hours: Mon-Fri 6:00 AM-6:00 PM; call center Mon-Fri 7:00 AM-5:00 PM
Funding Source: Not specified (operates under Title II ADA compliance; also accepts Medicaid/Medicaid Waiver/Medicare/Managed Care as payer sources alongside cash fares)
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public demand-response covering six southeast Indiana counties; reservations accepted up to 30 days in advance, first-come first-served. Decatur County receives Catch-A-Ride service only (not Lifetime Resources' other programs).

Name: MAPS (Metro Area Public Transit System)
Region/Service Area: Joplin, Webb City, Oronogo, Carterville, Duquesne, and Duenweg, MO
Fare: $4.00 full fare; $2.00 half fare (seniors 60+, military/veterans, persons with disabilities, Medicare); $2.00 teen fare; $1.00 child (under 12)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Curb-to-curb, prescheduled demand-response covering the greater Joplin metro area, open to the general public; separate paratransit tier serves ADA-eligible riders within 3/4 mile of the fixed bus route. Booking via joplinportal.maps-transit.com or phone.

Name: SMTS (Southeast Missouri Transportation Service)
Region/Service Area: 21 counties in Southeast and South Central Missouri (Bollinger, Butler, Carter, Crawford, Dent, Howell, Iron, Madison, New Madrid, Oregon, Pemiscot, Perry, Phelps, Reynolds, Shannon, St. Francois, Ste. Genevieve, Stoddard, Texas, Washington, Wayne)
Fare: Not specified (site states fare depends on program eligibility; no flat fare published)
Funding Source: Not specified (nonprofit; approved Medicaid provider; also serves Area Agencies on Aging and other institutional contracts alongside general-public rides)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Door-to-door and some fixed-route service marketed as 'Transportation For Everyone' / 'rural public transportation for everyone' across 21 SE Missouri counties, riders call their local SMTS office to schedule. Also provides Medicaid/NEMT trips as a separate funding stream -- the general-public demand-response tier is the basis for inclusion here.

Name: CGCTA Demand Response
Fare: Fare varies by trip distance; seniors 60+ ride free within Cape Girardeau County
Service Hours: Mon-Thu 5:00 AM-10:00 PM; Fri-Sat 5:00 AM-12:00 AM; Sun 5:00 AM-2:00 PM
Launch Year: Not specified (organization describes itself as having 'over 25 years of service')
Ridership/Performance Notes: Demand-response offered alongside CGCTA's fixed routes; requires 24-hour advance phone reservation. ELIGIBILITY IS AMBIGUOUS across sources: one CGCTA page frames it around 'seniors, individuals with disabilities, and those living in areas with limited fixed-route service,' while the fare structure (a standard fare plus a separate senior-free tier) implies general-public access. Included per the general-public-eligible reading but flagged for human verification -- see concerns.csv.

Name: VANLNK
Fleet: Smaller vehicles than standard StarTran buses; wheelchair-accessible
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launched April 20, 2020 as a pilot originally designed for disabled/senior riders; broadened to all residents citywide. Door-to-door, app-based on-demand booking anywhere within Lincoln city limits. A separate paratransit-eligible tier can now book up to 7 days in advance through the same app (2025 update) -- that advance option is for ADA-certified riders specifically; the general-public service remains same-day/on-demand.

Name: CRANE Public Transit
Region/Service Area: Grand Island Urbanized Area, NE, plus Alda, Wood River, Cairo, and Doniphan
Operator: Brown Transit, Inc. (contracted by the City of Grand Island)
Fare: $2.00 per one-way trip (CRANE Trip Card scanned on boarding)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Portal-to-portal demand-response open to the general public, 'no membership required'; minimum 24-hour advance reservation, same-day rides only if capacity permits. Approximately 38,000-42,000 trips/year.

Name: TeleLift (North Fork Area Transit)
Region/Service Area: Norfolk, Madison, Meadow Grove, Newman Grove, and Battle Creek, NE (Madison County); service reduced to Norfolk city limits as of July 2025 per a 30% state-funding cut
Fare: In-town fares start at $2.00 with 24-hour advance reservation; higher fares for county trips and same-day requests
Service Hours: Mon-Fri 7:00 AM-5:00 PM (hours effective July 1, 2025; reservation line Mon-Fri 8:00 AM-4:00 PM)
Funding Source: City of Norfolk, Norfolk United Way, Northeast Community College, local business sponsors, and Nebraska state funding (reduced ~30% per a 2025 service-hours notice)
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public dial-a-ride operating 3 routes/74 stops within a 30-mile radius of Norfolk; no senior/disability eligibility restriction found. Also operates a separate Regional Flex Route 6 (Norfolk-Wayne) which is a fixed-route-with-deviation service and is NOT included here as it fits this project's route-deviation exclusion.

Name: North Platte Public Transit
Region/Service Area: City of North Platte, NE and a 20-mile radius (incl. Lake Maloney, Indian Hills, Sutherland, Hershey, Maxwell)
Fare: $1.50-$2.00 one-way in-city with advance reservation; $4.00 for same-day reservation; $5.00-$10.00 per direction for extended/outside-city-limits trips (Sutherland, Hershey, Maxwell up to $10)
Service Hours: Mon-Sat (phone lines close 1 hour before end of service)
Funding Source: Not specified (City of North Platte sponsored)
Ridership/Performance Notes: General-public dial-a-ride ('available to everyone in North Platte and now anyone within a 20 mile radius'); offers both advance-reserved and same-day (higher-fare) trips, hence classified Scheduling Window = Flexible.

Name: Columbus Area Transit (CAT)
Fare: Punch cards: 5 rides/$10 or 10 rides/$20 (~$2/ride); discounted cards available for eligible riders
Funding Source: Nebraska Department of Transportation (Roads), United Way, City of Columbus budget
Ridership/Performance Notes: Curb-to-curb demand-response 'available to the general public regardless of race, ethnicity, age, sex, or disability' within Columbus city limits; riders must register and schedule at least one day in advance.

Name: Fremont Transit Program
Region/Service Area: City of Fremont, NE plus 2 miles beyond city limits (Dodge County)
Fare: $2.00 one-way when reserved 48+ hours in advance; $5.00 for same-day or under-48-hour reservations
Launch Year: Not specified (program described as launched 'September 7', year not confirmed)
Funding Source: FTA Section 5311 Rural Public Transportation grant
Ridership/Performance Notes: Door-to-door demand-response explicitly described as available to 'the general public, older adults and persons with disabilities.' One secondary source's framing ('for people whose disabilities prevent them from using fixed-route bus') conflicts with the general-public framing found elsewhere on the same city site; the general-public eligibility language is treated as controlling here per project convention, but flagged for verification.

Name: Blue Rivers Public Transportation
Region/Service Area: Gage, Jefferson, Nemaha, Otoe, and Thayer counties, NE (61 communities); plus 2 inter-city routes to Lincoln and Omaha
Operator: Blue Rivers Area Agency on Aging
Service Hours: Varies by office (e.g. Beatrice Mon-Fri 8:00 AM-12:00 PM, 12:30-4:30 PM; Auburn, Nebraska City, Fairbury, Hebron, Syracuse each with distinct local hours)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Demand-response, portal-to-portal service explicitly 'available to the public, including persons with disabilities' across a 5-county southeast Nebraska region; 24-hour advance reservation required. Also operates regular routed service connecting 61 communities plus 2 fixed inter-city routes (Lincoln, Omaha) -- those fixed-route pieces are not the basis for inclusion here, only the demand-response tier.

Name: SpartaGo
Region/Service Area: Spartanburg northside and southside neighborhoods, City of Spartanburg
Operator: City of Spartanburg / Spartanburg Area Regional Transit Agency (SPARTA)
Fare: $2.00 per rider (credit or debit card only)
Service Hours: 6:00 AM-6:00 PM, seven days a week
Funding Source: State (mass transit funds, vehicle purchase); Federal (COVID-era federal transit funds, pilot operations)
Fleet: 3 ADA-compliant Ford Transit chassis Mobilitytrans conversion vans
Ridership/Performance Notes: App-based direct pickup/dropoff similar to Uber/Lyft, serving Spartanburg's northside and southside neighborhoods only (not citywide). One-year pilot with a six-month evaluation checkpoint. Vehicle purchase cost ~$344,803; estimated pilot program cost ~$334,442.

Name: PDRTA Demand Response
Region/Service Area: Chesterfield, Darlington, Dillon, Florence, Marion, and Marlboro counties (Pee Dee region), SC — named zones include MARTi (Marlboro Co.), DCAT (Dillon Co.), Marion County, Chesterfield East, and Lower Florence
Fare: Fare-free (per PDRTA's 2026 service-change notices for converted routes)
Service Hours: Weekdays (varies by zone), approx. 8:00 AM-5:00 PM
Ridership/Performance Notes: Call-ahead (24-hour advance), door-to-door demand response distinct from PDRTA's ADA complementary paratransit. PDRTA's news page shows an active pattern of converting former fixed/commuter routes to this call-ahead model (Chesterfield East 5/1/26; Pamplico-Florence Commuter and MUSC Black River for Lower Florence 4/28/26). A 2024 press release with The Routing Company (Pingo platform) described a planned 'commingled paratransit and on-demand' + workforce-transit deployment, but no live app-based branding was found in PDRTA's own 2026 news archive, so Technology Vendor is left Not specified rather than naming Pingo/TRC.

Name: Santee Wateree RTA On-Demand (Sumter)
Region/Service Area: City of Sumter, SC (former Routes 50, 60, 100 corridors: West Liberty St., South Main St., East Liberty St.)
Service Hours: Monday-Friday 6:00 AM-6:00 PM (same-day reservation cutoff 4:00 PM)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Replaced three former fixed routes with a call-ahead, designated-stop on-demand zone service in Sumter (confirmed via SWRTA's own Facebook post; no eligibility restriction stated). SWRTA's separate services page describes a broader 'demand response' offering in Kershaw/Lee/Sumter counties in vaguer terms ('county residents...on a space available basis as a cash passenger') without confirming booking method or fare — this row covers only the confirmed Sumter on-demand zone service; the broader county-wide program may warrant separate follow-up.

Name: Aiken County 5311 Rural Transportation
Region/Service Area: Aiken County, SC (outside the urbanized area)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Distinct from Aiken Senior Life Services' other eligibility-restricted offerings (Dial-A-Ride for disabled riders; Title XIX/Medicaid transport) — this program is open to any resident living outside Aiken County's urbanized area, not senior/disability-gated. Trips must be scheduled at least 5 business days in advance; service area is 'anywhere within Aiken County.'

Name: Peach Blossom Express
Ridership/Performance Notes: Operator describes the service as meeting 'the transportation needs of all Edgefield County residents' — general public, not senior/disability-restricted despite the operator being the county Senior Citizens Council (same inclusion logic as Bamberg County's Handy Ride, already in this database). Listed on SCDOT's statewide transit-provider directory.

Name: Chester Connector (ChescoConnect)
Region/Service Area: Chester County, SC, with expanded coverage into Union County
Operator: The Connector (Senior Services, Inc. of Chester County), 501(c)(3) nonprofit
Fare: Not specified (described as 'low-cost'; discounted rates for seniors 65+, ADA-eligible riders 18-64, and Medicaid recipients; general-public riders pay full fare)
Service Hours: Monday-Friday, plus Saturday within Chester County; office hours Mon-Fri 8:00 AM-4:30 PM
Launch Year: 1973 (organization founded; demand-response service start date not separately confirmed)
Fleet: 15 vans; ~170 trips/day average reported by operator
Ridership/Performance Notes: Curb-to-curb demand response confirmed open to anyone age 12+ via the operator's own 'Who Can Ride' page (chesco.org/5326/Who-Can-Ride): general-public riders pay full fare while seniors/ADA-eligible/Medicaid riders receive reduced or program-funded rates. Not restricted to a certified eligibility class.

Name: York County Access
Region/Service Area: York County and City of Rock Hill, SC (Ride-to-Work limited to Rock Hill city limits)
Operator: York County Council on Aging (in cooperation with York County and City of Rock Hill)
Service Hours: Essential Service Mon-Fri 6:00 AM-6:00 PM; Ride-to-Work Mon-Fri 5:30-9:00 AM and 3:30-6:00 PM
Ridership/Performance Notes: Confirmed general public eligibility (residents of York County/Rock Hill) via operator's own county government page. 'Essential Service' (48-hr advance) covers medical-related trips countywide; 'Ride-to-Work' (24-hr advance) covers employment trips within Rock Hill. Its role is expanding following Rock Hill's May 2026 shutdown of its fixed-route MyRide bus system, per WBTV coverage.

Name: RPT GO
Region/Service Area: South Rochester, MN microtransit zone (bounded south of 12th St SE, west of 50th Ave SE, east of Badger Run Creek; hubs at Cub Foods SE, RCTC, Mayo High School, Quarry Hill Park, Fairgrounds Park & Ride; expanded 2026 to include Central Park)
Technology Vendor: Spare (Spare Labs) -- inferred from Google Play package name com.sparelabs.platform.rider.rptgo, not independently confirmed on the city's own site
Fare: $3.00 per ride; free for children under 5
Fleet: Electric mid-size SUVs and hybrid-fuel vans, wheelchair accessible
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launched October 2024 as a one-year pilot (through September 2025); pilot concluded on schedule and the city expanded the zone afterward rather than ending it, per a March 2026 service update. Distinct from Rochester's ZIPS Paratransit, which is eligibility-restricted to riders with disabilities and out of scope.

Name: goMARTI
Region/Service Area: 20-square-mile Grand Rapids, MN service area with ~70 pickup/dropoff points; by 2025 expanded to connect Grand Rapids with rural and tribal communities along Highway 2
Operator: City of Grand Rapids / Minnesota Department of Transportation (MnDOT), public-private partnership
Technology Vendor: Via (goMARTI 2.0 platform); originally launched on May Mobility's autonomous-vehicle platform
Service Hours: Monday-Saturday 10:00am-9:00pm, Sunday 8:00am-3:00pm (subject to change for weather/maintenance)
Funding Source: State (MnDOT), Local (City of Grand Rapids), Private (May Mobility, The PLUM Catalyst partnership)
Fleet: 9 vehicles: autonomous shuttles (May Mobility) with onboard human safety operator, plus electric vans (Volkswagen ID.Buzz being tested); 5 of 9 equipped with wheelchair ramps
Ridership/Performance Notes: Launched October 2022 as one of the first rural/tribal-community autonomous-vehicle transit pilots in the US; original 18-month pilot passed a 10,000-rider milestone and a later count cited 35,000 total rides; evolved into "goMARTI 2.0," combining AV shuttles with conventional electric-van service and expanding toward rural/tribal communities along Highway 2. MnDOT's 2025 CGMC presentation on goMARTI 2.0 could not be text-extracted (PDF rendered as binary/encoded) -- worth a follow-up read for expansion specifics.

Name: STA Link
Region/Service Area: Spokane County, WA — planned pilot zones: North Spokane Valley, Latah Valley, Liberty Lake, West Plains, Northeast Spokane (incl. Mead)
Operator: Spokane Transit Authority (contracted operator: Direct Medical Transportation, Inc.)
Fare: Expected to mirror STA standard bus fare (~$2.00 standard, $1.00 reduced) — not yet finalized at time of research
Launch Year: 2026 (planned, fall 2026 launch; not yet operating at time of research)
Funding Source: Local (Spokane Transit Authority; flat hourly rate contract with operator)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Announced mobility-on-demand pilot supplementing STA's fixed-route and ADA paratransit service, part of the Connect 2035 strategic plan; riders matched into shared rides of 1-5 passengers; includes a separate accessible-van overlay for seniors/mobility-impaired riders alongside the general-public service. Not yet launched as of this research (cleared for fall 2026 launch beginning with North Spokane Valley and Latah Valley zones).

Name: The Current (C-TRAN)
Region/Service Area: Clark County, WA — zones: WSU Vancouver/Salmon Creek, Rose Village, Camas/Washougal, Port of Vancouver, Ridgefield/La Center, Battle Ground
Fare: $1.50 adult; $0.75 honored; free for youth 18 and under (Youth Opportunity Pass)
Service Hours: Most zones: weekdays 5:30am-7:00pm, weekends 8:00am-6:00pm; Port of Vancouver weekdays only 5:30am-7:00pm
Ridership/Performance Notes: Point-to-point on-demand rideshare at bus-fare cost; riders arrive 5 minutes early, drivers wait up to 2 minutes; Hop Fastpass or cash accepted.

Name: Kitsap Transit On-Demand (Ride Pingo)
Region/Service Area: Kitsap County, WA — zones: BI Ride (Bainbridge Island), Kingston Ride + Fast Ferry Commuter, SK Ride (South Kitsap), Purdy Ride, Nollwood Dial-A-Ride
Fare: $2.00 general public; $1.00 seniors (62+), people with disabilities, youth (17 and under)
Service Hours: Varies by zone; SK Ride weekdays only; other zones include weekend/Sunday on-demand service
Ridership/Performance Notes: Kitsap Transit was reported as the first US transit agency to launch a paid pilot with The Routing Company (2021); on-demand or up-to-7-days-advance booking available depending on zone; Kingston Ride Fast Ferry Commuter variant requires booking by 4pm the day before. Combines several named on-demand zones under one shared app/program, similar in structure to King County Metro Flex and Community Transit Zip Shuttle, both already in this database as single multi-zone rows.

Name: CONNECT (Ben Franklin Transit)
Region/Service Area: Tri-Cities, WA — zones: Central Kennewick & Finley, Columbia Center & South Richland, West Richland & Badger Mountain, Central Richland, West Pasco, East Pasco
Fare: $1.50 per ride; first two rides free for new users; 10-ride tickets and monthly/senior/youth/veteran passes accepted
Funding Source: State (Washington Climate Commitment Act), Local (Ben Franklin Transit)
Ridership/Performance Notes: On-demand rideshare connecting riders to BFT's fixed-route network across 6 zones; 3-hour transfer window with fixed-route service.

Name: DART (Link Transit)
Ridership/Performance Notes: Shared-ride, advance-reservation dial-a-ride open to the general public within Leavenworth city limits; distinct from Link Transit's fixed-route network.

Name: DART (Grant Transit Authority)
Region/Service Area: Grant County, WA — Wilson Creek, Royal City, Mattawa, Ephrata, Soap Lake, Coulee City, Electric City, Grand Coulee
Ridership/Performance Notes: Shared-ride dial-a-ride explicitly for 'all persons' in listed small towns for trips not served by a regular fixed-route bus; distinct from GTA's separate ACCESS (ADA-certified) paratransit program.

Name: HarborFlex (Dial-A-Ride)
Region/Service Area: Grays Harbor County, WA — Montesano, Elma, Westport, Tokeland (weekdays), Ocean Shores (weekdays and weekends)
Service Hours: Varies by zone, approx. 7:30am-5:15pm; excludes 6 federal holidays
Ridership/Performance Notes: HarborFlex brand combines a certified ADA paratransit service with a general-public dial-a-ride (successor to the former 'Dial-A-Ride'); only the general-public dial-a-ride component is in scope here — trips bookable up to a week in advance via app or dispatch phone line.

Ridership/Performance Notes: Door-to-door dial-a-ride explicitly open to general public rural residents in the service area (not restricted to enrolled tribal members); rides for medical appointments, shopping, and quality-of-life trips; should be scheduled a few days in advance.

Operator: East Central Iowa Council of Governments (ECICOG); six county-based providers: Benton County Transportation, Iowa County Transportation, Johnson County SEATS, Jones County JETS, Linn County LIFTS, Washington County Minibus

Ridership/Performance Notes: General public service (riders under 16 must be accompanied by an adult 18+); confirmed via operator's own page. Rides bookable up to 7 days in advance with a 30-minute pickup window, using the Via-powered app/web platform (horizons.app.ridewithvia.com). Operates during hours when Cedar Rapids' fixed-route buses do not run, effectively a gap-filler on-demand service across three cities.
